title.en: Volume 398 Biographies 157: Yu Duanli, Li Bi, Qiu Chong, Ni Si, Yu Wenshaojie, Li Fan
title.raw: 卷三百九十八 列傳第一百五十七 余端禮 李壁 丘崈 倪思 宇文紹節 李蘩 Volume 398 Biographies 157: Yu Duanli, Li Bi, Qiu Chong, Ni Si, Yu Wenshaojie, Li Fan

sentences.zh: 余端禮

translations.literal: Yu Duanli
translations.idiomatic: Yu Duanli

sentences.zh: 余端禮，字處恭，衢州龍遊人。

translations.literal: Yu Duanli, courtesy name Chugong, was a native of Longyou in Quzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Duanli, whose courtesy name was Chugong, came from Longyou in Quzhou.

sentences.zh: 第進士，知湖州烏程縣。

translations.literal: He placed as a jinshi and served as magistrate of Wucheng County in Huzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After passing the jinshi examination, he was appointed magistrate of Wucheng County in Huzhou.

sentences.zh: 民間賦丁絹錢，率三氓出一縑，不輸絹而折其估，一縑千錢，後增至五千，民不勝病。

translations.literal: Among the people there was a poll tax in silk cash: as a rule three commoners supplied one bolt of silk; if they did not deliver silk the assessment was commuted, one bolt being valued at a thousand cash, later raised to five thousand, and the people could not bear the hardship.
translations.idiomatic: The people were assessed a poll tax payable in silk money, with three households typically required to furnish one bolt. Those who did not pay in silk had the levy converted to a cash equivalent—initially one thousand cash per bolt, later raised to five thousand—and the burden became unbearable.

sentences.zh: 端禮以告於府，事得上聞，又自詣中書陳便宜，歲蠲緡錢六萬。

translations.literal: Duanli reported this to the prefectural office; the matter reached the throne, and he also went in person to the Secretariat to set forth what would be advantageous, and each year sixty thousand strings of cash were remitted.
translations.idiomatic: Duanli reported the abuse to the prefecture, and the case was brought to the court’s attention. He then went to the Secretariat in person to argue for relief, securing an annual remission of sixty thousand strings of cash.

sentences.zh: 召對，時孝宗志在恢復，端禮言：

translations.literal: He was summoned for an audience; at that time Emperor Xiaozong’s will was set on recovery, and Duanli said:
translations.idiomatic: When he was summoned to audience, Emperor Xiaozong was intent on reconquest. Duanli said:

sentences.zh: 「謀敵決勝之道，有聲有實。

translations.literal: “The way to plot against an enemy and decide victory has both show and substance.
translations.idiomatic: “The art of defeating an enemy combines display and substance.

sentences.zh: 敵弱者先聲後實，以讋其氣；

translations.literal: When the enemy is weak, first show then substance, to cow his spirit;
translations.idiomatic: Against a weak foe, put show before substance to break his morale;

sentences.zh: 敵強者先實後聲，以俟其機。

translations.literal: when the enemy is strong, first substance then show, to await the opportune moment.
translations.idiomatic: against a strong foe, put substance before show and wait for the right moment.

sentences.zh: 漢武乘匈奴之困，親行邊陲，威震朔方，而漠南無王庭者，讋其氣而服之，所謂先聲而後實也。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Han, taking advantage of the Xiongnu’s distress, personally toured the frontier; his might shook the north, and south of the desert there was no royal court—he cowed their spirit and they submitted; this is what is called first show and then substance.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Han exploited the Xiongnu’s weakness, toured the borderlands in person, and awed the northern frontier until no royal court remained south of the desert. He subdued their spirit and won their submission—true “show before substance.”

sentences.zh: 越謀吳則不然，外講盟好，內修武備，陽行成以種、蠡，陰結援于齊、晉，教習之士益精，而獻遺之禮益密，用能一戰而霸者，伺其機而圖之，所謂先實而後聲也。

translations.literal: When Yue plotted against Wu it was otherwise: outwardly they negotiated alliance, inwardly they trained arms; openly they made peace through Wen Zhong and Fan Li, secretly they secured aid from Qi and Jin; drilled troops grew ever sharper and tribute gifts ever more frequent, and thus with one battle they achieved hegemony—watching for the moment and scheming accordingly; this is what is called first substance and then show.
translations.idiomatic: Yue’s campaign against Wu was different: outwardly it cultivated alliance while inwardly it sharpened arms; Wen Zhong and Fan Li publicly sued for peace even as secret ties were forged with Qi and Jin. Drill grew ever stricter and tribute ever more lavish, until a single battle won hegemony—watching the moment and striking accordingly, the classic case of “substance before show.”

sentences.zh: 今日之事異於漢而與越相若。

translations.literal: Today’s affair differs from Han and resembles Yue.
translations.idiomatic: Our situation today differs from Han Wu’s case and resembles Yue’s against Wu.

sentences.zh: 願陰設其備，而密為之謀，觀變察時，則機可投矣。

translations.literal: I wish that preparations be set up in secret and plans laid covertly; observing changes and discerning the season, then the opportune moment may be seized.
translations.idiomatic: I urge that we prepare in secret and plot in silence, watching shifts and reading the times—then the moment to strike may be seized.

sentences.zh: 古之投機者有四：有投隙之機，有搗虛之機，有乘亂之機，有承弊之機。

translations.literal: Those who seized opportune moments in antiquity had four kinds: the moment of striking a gap, the moment of raiding an opening, the moment of exploiting disorder, and the moment of pressing an exhausted foe.
translations.idiomatic: Ancient strategists recognized four kinds of opportunity: striking a gap, raiding an undefended point, exploiting disorder, and pressing a spent enemy.

sentences.zh: 因其內釁而擊之，若匈奴困於三國之攻而宣帝出師，此投隙之機也。

translations.literal: Striking because of internal strife, as when the Xiongnu were harried by the attacks of the Three Kingdoms and Emperor Xuan marched out—this is the moment of striking a gap.
translations.idiomatic: To attack when internal strife opens a breach—as when the Xiongnu were worn down by the Three Kingdoms’ assaults and Emperor Xuan took the field—is to seize a gap.

sentences.zh: 因其外患而伐之，若夫差牽于黃池之役而越兵入吳，此搗虛之機也。

translations.literal: Invading because of external troubles, as when Fuchai was tied down at the Battle of Huangchi and Yue troops entered Wu—this is the moment of raiding an opening.
translations.idiomatic: To invade when an external crisis distracts the foe—as when King Fuchai was pinned at Huangchi and Yue armies poured into Wu—is to raid an opening.

sentences.zh: 敵國不道，因其離而舉之，若晉之降孫皓，此乘亂之機也。

translations.literal: When a hostile state is without the Way, rising because it is divided, as when Jin received the surrender of Sun Hao—this is the moment of exploiting disorder.
translations.idiomatic: When a rival state loses the Way and splits apart, to rise against its divisions—as when Jin accepted Sun Hao’s surrender—is to exploit disorder.

sentences.zh: 敵人勢窮，躡其後而蹙之，若高祖之追項羽，此乘弊之機也。

translations.literal: When the enemy’s strength is spent, following on his heels and pressing him, as when Gaozu pursued Xiang Yu—this is the moment of pressing an exhausted foe.
translations.idiomatic: When the enemy’s power is exhausted, to follow hard on his heels and hem him in—as when Gaozu pursued Xiang Yu—is to press a spent foe.

sentences.zh: 機之未至，不可以先；

translations.literal: When the moment has not arrived, one must not act ahead of it;
translations.idiomatic: Before the moment arrives, one must not move too soon;

sentences.zh: 機之已至，不可以後。

translations.literal: when the moment has arrived, one must not lag behind.
translations.idiomatic: once it has arrived, one must not lag behind.

sentences.zh: 以此備邊，安若太山，以此應敵，動如破竹，惟所欲為，無不如志。」

translations.literal: With this to prepare the border, secure as Mount Tai; with this to meet the enemy, moving like splitting bamboo—whatever you wish to do, nothing will fail to accord with your will.”
translations.idiomatic: Use this to secure the frontier and the realm will stand firm as Mount Tai; use it to meet the enemy and your advance will cleave like bamboo. Whatever you undertake will succeed.”

sentences.zh: 上喜曰：「卿可謂通事體矣。」

translations.literal: The emperor said with pleasure: “You may be said to understand how affairs stand.”
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said with delight, “You truly grasp how affairs stand.”

sentences.zh: 後以薦為監察御史，遷大理少卿，轉太常少卿。

translations.literal: Later, on recommendation, he was made investigating censor, promoted to vice minister of justice, and transferred to vice minister of rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was later recommended as investigating censor, promoted to vice minister of justice, and then transferred to vice minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 詔以來歲祈穀上帝，仲春躬耕籍田，令禮官討論明道故事。

translations.literal: An edict ordered that in the coming year prayers for grain be offered to the Supreme Lord, that in mid-spring the emperor personally plow the sacred field, and that ritual officials study the precedents of the Mingdao reign.
translations.idiomatic: An edict directed that the following year the court should pray for grain to the Supreme Lord and that the emperor should personally plow the sacred field in mid-spring, and it ordered ritual officials to review the precedents of the Mingdao period.

sentences.zh: 端禮言：「祈穀之制，合祭天地於圜丘，前期享於太廟，視冬至郊祀之儀，此國朝故事也。

translations.literal: Duanli said: “The institution of praying for grain is a joint sacrifice to Heaven and Earth at the Circular Mound, with a prior offering at the Imperial Ancestral Temple, following the rites of the winter solstice suburban sacrifice—this is our dynasty’s established practice.
translations.idiomatic: Duanli said, “The rite of praying for grain calls for a joint sacrifice to Heaven and Earth at the Circular Mound, with a preliminary offering at the Imperial Ancestral Temple, following the same protocol as the winter solstice suburban sacrifice. That is our dynasty’s established practice.

sentences.zh: 若乃明道之制，則以宮中火後考室落成，故于太安殿恭謝天地，此特一時謝災之事耳。

translations.literal: As for the Mingdao institution, it was because after a fire in the palace the ancestral hall was completed, and therefore thanks were offered to Heaven and Earth in the Hall of Great Peace—this was merely a one-time ceremony of thanksgiving for deliverance from calamity.
translations.idiomatic: The Mingdao precedent arose only because, after a palace fire, the ancestral hall was completed and thanks were offered to Heaven and Earth in the Hall of Great Peace—a one-time ceremony of thanksgiving for deliverance from disaster.

sentences.zh: 今欲祈穀而耕籍，必合祭天地於圜丘，必前期朝享于景靈宮、太廟可也。

translations.literal: Now, wishing to pray for grain and plow the sacred field, one must jointly sacrifice to Heaven and Earth at the Circular Mound, and beforehand perform the court offering at the Jingling Palace and the Imperial Ancestral Temple—that will do.
translations.idiomatic: If we are to pray for grain and plow the sacred field now, we must sacrifice jointly at the Circular Mound and hold the preliminary court offerings at the Jingling Palace and the Imperial Ancestral Temple.

sentences.zh: 欲如明道之制，行於殿庭不可。」

translations.literal: To wish to follow the Mingdao institution and perform it in the palace hall is not permissible.”
translations.idiomatic: To follow the Mingdao precedent and perform the rite in the palace hall is unacceptable.”

sentences.zh: 詔太常、禮部集議。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and the Ministry of Rites to assemble for deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and the Ministry of Rites to deliberate jointly.

sentences.zh: 中書有可以義起者，端禮曰：「禮固有可義起，至於大體，則不可易。

translations.literal: In the Secretariat there were those who held that rites might be initiated by expediency; Duanli said: “Rites indeed may sometimes be initiated by expediency, but as to the great framework, it cannot be altered.
translations.idiomatic: Some at the Secretariat argued that rites could be improvised where expedient. Duanli said, “Rites may sometimes be initiated by expediency, but the fundamental framework must not be changed.

sentences.zh: 古者郊而後耕，以其於郊，故謂之郊，猶祀於明堂，故謂之明堂。

translations.literal: In antiquity one sacrificed at the suburban altar and then plowed; because it was at the suburban altar, it was called the suburban sacrifice; just as when sacrificing in the Bright Hall, it was called the Bright Hall.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity the suburban sacrifice preceded the plowing; because it took place at the suburban altar, it was called the suburban rite, just as sacrifice in the Bright Hall was called the Bright Hall rite.

sentences.zh: 如明道謝災之制，則與祈穀異。

translations.literal: Such as the Mingdao institution of thanksgiving for calamity—that differs from praying for grain.
translations.idiomatic: The Mingdao thanksgiving for disaster is a different rite altogether from praying for grain.

sentences.zh: 今以郊而施之殿庭，亦將以明堂而施之壇壝乎？

translations.literal: Now to apply the suburban sacrifice in the palace hall—is one also to apply the Bright Hall rite to the altar mounds?
translations.idiomatic: If we now perform the suburban rite in the palace hall, shall we also perform the Bright Hall rite on the altar mounds?

sentences.zh: 禮之失自端禮始，端禮死不敢奉詔。」

translations.literal: The lapse in ritual would begin with Duanli; Duanli would rather die than obey the edict.”
translations.idiomatic: If ritual is corrupted, let the blame begin with me—I would rather die than obey such an edict.”

sentences.zh: 上為之止。

translations.literal: The emperor stopped the plan on his account.
translations.idiomatic: On this the emperor abandoned the plan.

sentences.zh: 權兵部侍郎兼太子詹事，進吏部侍郎，出知太平州，奉祠。

translations.literal: He served as acting vice minister of war and concurrently grand mentor of the heir apparent, was promoted to vice minister of personnel, went out as prefect of Taiping, and received a sinecure appointment.
translations.idiomatic: He served as acting vice minister of war and concurrently grand mentor of the heir apparent, was promoted to vice minister of personnel, was sent out as prefect of Taiping, and later held a sinecure post.

sentences.zh: 光宗立，召見，言：「天子之孝不與庶人同。

translations.literal: When Emperor Guangzong ascended, he was summoned for audience and said: “The Son of Heaven’s filial piety is not the same as that of commoners.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Guangzong took the throne, Duanli was summoned and said, “A Son of Heaven’s filial duty is not the same as a commoner’s.

sentences.zh: 今陛下之孝于壽皇，當如舜之於堯，行其道可也，武之于文，繼其志、述其事可也。

translations.literal: Your Majesty’s filial piety toward Shouhuang should be like Shun toward Yao—putting his Way into practice will suffice; like King Wu toward King Wen—continuing his will and carrying on his undertakings will suffice.
translations.idiomatic: Your filial duty to Shouhuang should be like Shun’s to Yao—carry forward his Way; like King Wu’s to King Wen—continue his aims and complete his work.

sentences.zh: 凡壽皇睿謀聖訓，仁政善教，所嘗施於天下者，願與二三大臣朝夕講求而力行之，則足以盡事親之孝矣。」

translations.literal: All of Shouhuang’s sagely counsels and holy instructions, benevolent policies and excellent teachings that were once applied throughout the realm—I wish that together with the chief ministers you study them morning and evening and strive to put them into practice; that will suffice to fulfill the filial piety of serving one’s parent.”
translations.idiomatic: All of Shouhuang’s wise policies and sage teachings, the benevolent measures once applied across the realm—I urge Your Majesty to study them day and night with your leading ministers and put them vigorously into practice. That is how you will fully honor a father’s legacy.”

sentences.zh: 授集英殿修撰、知贛州，還為吏部侍郎、權刑部尚書兼侍講，以煥章閣直學士知建康府。

translations.literal: He was appointed compiler at the Hall for Assembling Excellence and prefect of Ganzhou; returning, he became vice minister of personnel, acting minister of justice and concurrently court lecturer, and as academician of the Huanzhang Pavilion was made prefect of Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed compiler at the Hall for Assembling Excellence and prefect of Ganzhou. On his return he served as vice minister of personnel and acting minister of justice while lecturing at court, and later as academician of the Huanzhang Pavilion and prefect of Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 召拜吏部尚書，擢同知樞密院事。

translations.literal: He was summoned and appointed minister of personnel, and promoted to associate commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled, appointed minister of personnel, and promoted to associate commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 興州帥吳挺死，端禮謂樞密趙汝愚曰：「吳氏世握蜀兵，今若復令承襲，將為後患。」

translations.literal: The commander of Xingzhou, Wu Ting, died; Duanli said to the military commissioner Zhao Ruyu: “The Wu clan has for generations held Sichuan’s armies; if they are again allowed to inherit the command, it will become a trouble for later.”
translations.idiomatic: When Wu Ting, military commissioner of Xingzhou, died, Duanli told Zhao Ruyu, military affairs commissioner, “The Wu family has held Sichuan’s armies for generations. If we let them inherit command again, we will breed future trouble.”

sentences.zh: 汝愚是其言，合辭以奏，光宗意未決，端禮言：「汝愚所請為蜀計，為東南計。

translations.literal: Zhao Ruyu agreed with his words; they joined memorials to present the case. Emperor Guangzong’s mind was not yet decided; Duanli said: “What Ruyu requests is a plan for Sichuan and a plan for the southeast.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Ruyu agreed and they submitted a joint memorial, but Guangzong hesitated. Duanli said, “Ruyu’s request is a plan for Sichuan—and for the southeast.

sentences.zh: 夫置大將而非其人，是無蜀也，無蜀，是無東南也。

translations.literal: To place a great general who is not the right man is to have no Sichuan; with no Sichuan, there is no southeast.
translations.idiomatic: To appoint a commander who is not fit is to lose Sichuan; lose Sichuan and you lose the southeast.

sentences.zh: 今軍中請帥而遲遲不報，人將生心。」

translations.literal: Now the army requests a commander and the court delays its reply—men will harbor other thoughts.”
translations.idiomatic: The army has asked for a commander and the court delays its answer—men will begin to scheme.”

sentences.zh: 不聽。

translations.literal: The emperor did not heed him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor would not listen.

sentences.zh: 後挺子曦卒以蜀叛，如端禮言。

translations.literal: Later Ting’s son Xi ultimately rebelled in Sichuan, just as Duanli had said.
translations.idiomatic: Later Wu Xi, Ting’s son, did rebel in Sichuan, exactly as Duanli had warned.

sentences.zh: 上以疾不朝重華宮，孝宗崩，又不能發喪，人情恟然。

translations.literal: The emperor, owing to illness, did not attend court at Chonghua Palace; when Emperor Xiaozong died he could not even proclaim the mourning, and popular feeling was in turmoil.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, ill, stopped attending court at Chonghua Palace. When Xiaozong died he could not even proclaim mourning, and public sentiment grew turbulent.

sentences.zh: 端禮謂宰相留正曰：「公獨不見唐肅宗朝群臣發哀太極殿故事乎？

translations.literal: Duanli said to the chief minister Liu Zheng: “Have you alone not seen the story of how in Emperor Suzong’s time of Tang the ministers proclaimed mourning at the Hall of Supreme Ultimate?
translations.idiomatic: Duanli said to Chief Minister Liu Zheng, “Have you forgotten how in Tang Suzong’s reign the ministers themselves proclaimed mourning at the Hall of Supreme Ultimate?

sentences.zh: 宜請太皇太后代行祭之禮。」

translations.literal: You should request that the Grand Empress Dowager perform the sacrificial rites in his stead.”
translations.idiomatic: You should ask the Grand Empress Dowager to perform the mourning rites in his stead.”

sentences.zh: 於是宰執以請于太皇太后，留正懼，入臨重華宮，仆地致仕而去。

translations.literal: Thereupon the chief ministers made the request of the Grand Empress Dowager; Liu Zheng, in fear, entered Chonghua Palace to attend the lying-in-state, fell prostrate, resigned office, and departed.
translations.idiomatic: The chief ministers then petitioned the Grand Empress Dowager. Liu Zheng, in fear, entered Chonghua Palace to attend the lying-in-state, collapsed, resigned, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 太皇太后垂簾，策皇子嘉王即皇帝位，王流涕遜避。

translations.literal: The Grand Empress Dowager held the curtain audience and designated the imperial prince, Prince Jia, to ascend the imperial throne; the prince wept, yielded, and shrank back.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Empress Dowager held court behind the curtain and designated Prince Jia, the imperial prince, to take the throne. The prince wept and shrank back in refusal.

sentences.zh: 端禮奏：「太上違豫，大喪乏主，安危之機在於呼吸，太皇太后非為陛下計，乃為太上皇帝計，為宗社計。

translations.literal: Duanli memorialized: “The Retired Emperor is gravely ill; the great mourning lacks a presiding lord; the hinge of safety and peril hangs on a breath. The Grand Empress Dowager is not acting for Your Majesty’s sake but for the Retired Emperor’s sake and for the altars of state.
translations.idiomatic: Duanli memorialized, “The Retired Emperor is gravely ill; the great mourning has no presiding lord; the realm’s safety hangs by a breath. The Grand Empress Dowager acts not for Your Majesty alone but for the Retired Emperor and for the altars of state.

sentences.zh: 今堅持退讓，不思國家之大計，是守匹夫之小節而昧天子之大孝也。」

translations.literal: Now to insist on yielding and not consider the great plan of the state is to keep a commoner’s petty scruple and be blind to a Son of Heaven’s great filial piety.”
translations.idiomatic: To cling to refusal now and ignore the state’s urgent need is to uphold a commoner’s petty scruple and miss a Son of Heaven’s greater filial duty.”

sentences.zh: 寧宗悚然收淚，不得已，側身就御坐之半。

translations.literal: Emperor Ningzong started in alarm, wiped away his tears, and with no alternative turned sideways and took half of the imperial seat.
translations.idiomatic: Ningzong started, dried his tears, and with no choice turned and took half of the imperial seat.

sentences.zh: 端禮與汝愚再拜固請，寧宗乃正御坐，退行禫祭禮。

translations.literal: Duanli and Ruyu bowed again and urgently pressed him; Ningzong then properly took the imperial seat and withdrew to perform the end-of-mourning sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Duanli and Zhao Ruyu bowed again and pressed him firmly until Ningzong took the full seat and withdrew to perform the end-of-mourning rites.

sentences.zh: 進端禮知樞密院事兼參知政事。

translations.literal: Duanli was advanced to commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs and concurrently participant in governance.
translations.idiomatic: Duanli was promoted to commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs and concurrently participant in governance.

sentences.zh: 汝愚去右丞相位，端禮代之。

translations.literal: Ruyu left the post of right chief councilor and Duanli replaced him.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhao Ruyu left the post of right chief councilor, Duanli replaced him.

sentences.zh: 始，端禮與汝愚同心共政，汝愚嘗曰：「士論未一，非余處恭不能任。」

translations.literal: At first Duanli and Ruyu shared the same mind in government; Ruyu once said: “Scholar-official opinion is not united—without Yu Chugong it cannot be borne.”
translations.idiomatic: At first Duanli and Zhao Ruyu governed in concert. Ruyu once said, “Scholar-official opinion is not united—without Yu Chugong the burden cannot be carried.”

sentences.zh: 及韓侂胄以傳道之勞，寖竊威柄，汝愚等欲疏斥之，謀泄而汝愚逐。

translations.literal: When Han Tuozhou, on account of his merit in conveying the succession, gradually usurped power, Ruyu and others wished to distance and expel him; the plot leaked and Ruyu was driven out.
translations.idiomatic: But Han Tuozhou, citing his role in securing the succession, gradually seized power. Ruyu and others tried to isolate him; the plot leaked and Ruyu was driven out.

sentences.zh: 端禮不能遏，但長籲而已。

translations.literal: Duanli could not restrain him and could only sigh long.
translations.idiomatic: Duanli could not check him and could only sigh.

sentences.zh: 浙西常平黃灝以放民租竄，知婺州黃度以庇蜀吏褫職罷郡，二人皆侂胄所憾，端禮執奏，竟不免於罪。

translations.literal: Huang Hao of the Zhexi Ever-Normal Granary was demoted for remitting the people’s rent; Huang Du, prefect of Wuzhou, was stripped of office and removed from his prefecture for shielding a Sichuan clerk—both men were objects of Tuozhou’s resentment; Duanli firmly memorialized, yet in the end they did not escape punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Hao of the Zhexi Ever-Normal Granary was demoted for remitting tenants’ rent; Huang Du, prefect of Wuzhou, was stripped of office for shielding a Sichuan clerk—both were men Han Tuozhou resented. Duanli memorialized firmly on their behalf, yet both were punished in the end.

sentences.zh: 太府丞呂祖儉坐上書忤侂胄南遷，端禮救解不獲，公議始歸責焉。

translations.literal: Lu Zujian, vice director of the Court of the Imperial Treasury, was banished south for a memorial that offended Tuozhou; Duanli sought to rescue him but did not succeed, and public opinion began to lay blame on him.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zujian of the Imperial Treasury was banished south for a memorial that offended Tuozhou. Duanli tried to save him and failed, and public opinion began to turn against Duanli.

sentences.zh: 他日見上，言除從官中書不知，朝綱已紊，禍根已滋。

translations.literal: Another day, seeing the emperor, he said that in appointing attendant officials the Secretariat did not know—court discipline was already disordered and the root of calamity already sprouting.
translations.idiomatic: On another audience he told the emperor that attendant officials were being appointed without the Secretariat’s knowledge—court discipline was already fraying and the seeds of disaster were sprouting.

sentences.zh: 即丐去，不許，進左丞相。

translations.literal: He immediately begged to leave office; this was not granted, and he was advanced to left chief councilor.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately asked to resign but was refused and was promoted to left chief councilor instead.

sentences.zh: 端禮在相位期年，頗知擁護善類，然為侂胄所制，壹鬱不愜志，稱疾求退，以觀文殿大學士提舉洞霄宮。

translations.literal: Duanli was in the chief councilor’s post for a year and was rather good at protecting worthy men, yet he was constrained by Tuozhou, deeply depressed and not content in mind; he claimed illness and sought to retire, and was made grand academician of the Hall for Viewing Literature to direct the Palace of Grotto Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Duanli served as chief councilor for a year and did much to protect worthy men, yet Han Tuozhou constrained him. Deeply frustrated, he pleaded illness and retired, becoming grand academician of the Hall for Viewing Literature and director of the Palace of Grotto Heaven.

sentences.zh: 居頃之，判潭州，移慶元，復帥潭。

translations.literal: After a short while he was assigned to Tanzhou, transferred to Qingyuan, and again commanded Tan.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he was assigned to Tanzhou, transferred to Qingyuan, and again given command of Tan.

sentences.zh: 薨，授少保、郇國公致仕，贈太傅，諡「忠肅」。

translations.literal: He died; he was granted Junior Guardian and made Lord of Yun in retirement, posthumously given Grand Mentor, with the posthumous title “Loyal and Solemn.”
translations.idiomatic: He died. In retirement he had held Junior Guardian and been enfeoffed as Lord of Yun; posthumously he was given Grand Mentor with the temple name Loyal and Solemn.

sentences.zh: 子嶸，工部尚書。

translations.literal: His son Song was minister of works.
translations.idiomatic: His son Song became minister of works.

sentences.zh: 李璧，字季章，眉之丹稜人。

translations.literal: Li Bi, courtesy name Jizhang, was a native of Danling in Mei.
translations.idiomatic: Li Bi, whose courtesy name was Jizhang, came from Danling in Mei Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 父燾，典國史。

translations.literal: His father Tao compiled the national history.
translations.idiomatic: His father Tao was in charge of compiling the national history.

sentences.zh: 壁少英悟，日誦萬餘言，屬辭精博，周必大見其文，異之曰：「此謫仙才也。」

translations.literal: Bi from youth was brilliantly perceptive; each day he recited more than ten thousand words; his compositions were refined and broad; Zhou Bida saw his writings and marveled, saying: “This is the talent of a banished immortal.”
translations.idiomatic: From youth Bi was exceptionally bright, reciting more than ten thousand characters a day and writing with refined breadth. Zhou Bida read his work and exclaimed, “This is the talent of a banished immortal.”

sentences.zh: 孝宗嘗問燾：「卿諸子孰可用？」

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaozong once asked Tao: “Among your sons, which can be employed?”
translations.idiomatic: Xiaozong once asked Tao, “Which of your sons is fit for service?”

sentences.zh: 燾以璧對。

translations.literal: Tao answered with Bi.
translations.idiomatic: Tao named Bi.

sentences.zh: 以父任入官，後登進士第。

translations.literal: He entered office by his father’s privilege and later passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: He entered office through his father’s privilege and later passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 召試，為正字。

translations.literal: He was summoned for examination and made corrector.
translations.idiomatic: Summoned for a palace examination, he was made a corrector.

sentences.zh: 璧受命使金，行次揚州，忠義人朱裕挾宋師襲漣水，金人憤甚，璧乞梟裕首境上，詔從其請。

translations.literal: Bi received orders as envoy to Jin; passing Yangzhou, the loyalist Zhu Yu, taking Song troops, raided Lianshui; the Jin people were greatly enraged; Bi begged that Yu’s head be displayed on the border, and an edict followed his request.
translations.idiomatic: Bi was dispatched as envoy to Jin. At Yangzhou he learned that the loyalist Zhu Yu had led Song troops in a raid on Lianshui, enraging the Jin court. Bi asked that Zhu’s head be displayed on the border, and the emperor granted his request.

sentences.zh: 璧至燕，與金人言，披露肝膽，金人之疑頓釋。

translations.literal: Bi reached Yan and spoke with the Jin people, laying bare his heart and liver; the Jin people’s suspicions were suddenly dispelled.
translations.idiomatic: When Bi reached Yan he spoke frankly with the Jin envoys, laying his cards on the table, and their suspicions quickly dissolved.

sentences.zh: 璧歸，侂胄用師意方銳，璧言：「進取之機，當重發而必至，毋輕出而苟沮。」

translations.literal: When Bi returned, Tuozhou’s intent to use troops was keen; Bi said: “The moment for advance should be launched with weight and must arrive—do not sally lightly and casually be discouraged.”
translations.idiomatic: On his return Han Tuozhou was eager for war. Bi said, “The moment to advance must be seized with full force and certainty—do not strike lightly and risk discouragement.”

sentences.zh: 既而陳景俊使北還，贊舉兵甚力，錢象祖以沮兵議忤侂胄得罪貶，璧論襄陽形勢，深以腹心為憂，欲待敵先發，然後應之，侂胄意不懌，於是四川、荊、淮各建宣撫而師出矣。

translations.literal: Soon after Chen Jingjun returned from mission north and strongly urged raising troops; Qian Xiangzu, for discouraging war, offended Tuozhou and was punished and demoted; Bi discussed the situation at Xiangyang, deeply worried about the heartland, wishing to wait until the enemy struck first and then respond—Tuozhou was displeased in mind, and thereupon Sichuan, Jing, and Huai each had pacification commissioners established and the armies marched out.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Chen Jingjun returned from the north urging war vigorously; Qian Xiangzu was punished for opposing it. Bi analyzed Xiangyang’s strategic position, warning that the heartland was exposed, and urged waiting for the enemy to move first—but Tuozhou was displeased. Pacification commissioners were then appointed for Sichuan, Jing, and Huai, and the armies marched.

sentences.zh: 璧度力不能回，乃入奏：「自秦檜首倡和議，使父兄百世之仇不復開于臣子之口。

translations.literal: Bi judged that his strength could not turn matters back and therefore entered to memorialize: “Since Qin Hui first advocated the peace agreement, he made the feud of a hundred generations between fathers and elder brothers no longer to be opened on ministers’ and sons’ lips.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing he could not turn policy back, Bi memorialized, “Ever since Qin Hui first championed peace, the feud our fathers and elder brothers bore for a hundred generations has been sealed from ministers’ lips.

sentences.zh: 今廟謀未定，士氣積衰，苟非激昂，曷克丕應。

translations.literal: Now court planning is not settled and military morale has long decayed; if we are not roused to ardor, how can we greatly respond?
translations.idiomatic: Court strategy is unsettled and morale has long decayed; without stirring ardor, how can we rise to the moment?

sentences.zh: 臣愚以為宜亟貶秦檜，示天下以讐恥必復之志，則宏綱舉而國論明，流俗變而人心一，君臣上下奮勵振作，拯潰民於殘虐，湔祖宗之宿憤。

translations.literal: Your servant foolishly holds that Qin Hui should quickly be demoted, showing the realm the will that feud and shame must be avenged; then the great framework will be raised and national discourse clarified, vulgar custom will change and hearts be united, ruler and ministers above and below will strive and rouse themselves, rescue the scattered people from cruel abuse, and wash away the ancestors’ long-standing resentment.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly urge that Qin Hui be swiftly degraded to show the realm our resolve to avenge feud and shame. Then the great framework will stand clear, public debate will align, custom will shift and hearts unite, ruler and ministers will rouse themselves, rescue the people from cruelty, and wash away our ancestors’ long resentment.

sentences.zh: 在今日舉而措之，無難矣。」

translations.literal: To raise it today and set it in place—there is no difficulty.”
translations.idiomatic: To act on this today would not be difficult.”

sentences.zh: 疏奏，秦檜坐追王爵。

translations.literal: When the memorial was presented, Qin Hui was punished by stripping his princely rank.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was presented, Qin Hui’s princely title was posthumously revoked.

sentences.zh: 議者謂璧不論檜之無君而但指其主和，其言雖公，特以迎合侂胄用兵之私而已。

translations.literal: Discussants said that Bi did not discuss Hui’s lack of loyalty to the ruler but only pointed to his advocacy of peace; though his words were public-spirited, they were merely to accommodate Tuozhou’s private wish to use troops.
translations.idiomatic: Critics said Bi attacked Hui only for advocating peace, not for disloyalty to the throne—his words sounded public-spirited but really catered to Tuozhou’s private wish for war.

sentences.zh: 初，侂胄召葉適直學士院，草出師詔，適不從，乃以屬璧，由是進權禮部尚書。

translations.literal: At first Tuozhou summoned Ye Shi to the Hanlin Academy to draft the expedition edict; Shi did not comply, and the task was therefore assigned to Bi; thereby he was advanced to acting minister of rites.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Tuozhou had summoned Ye Shi to draft the expedition edict; Ye refused, and the task fell to Bi, who was then promoted to acting minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 侂胄既喪師，始覺為蘇師旦所誤，一夕招璧飲，酒酣，及師旦事，璧微擿其過，覘侂胄意向，乃極言：「師旦怙勢招權，使明公負謗，非竄謫此人，不足以謝天下。」

translations.literal: After Tuozhou had lost his armies he first realized he had been misled by Su Shidan; one evening he invited Bi to drink; when the wine was warm they came to Shidan’s affair; Bi lightly plucked at his faults, gauging Tuozhou’s intent, and then spoke to the utmost: “Shidan relied on power to gather authority, causing Your Excellency to bear slander—unless this man is banished and demoted, it is not enough to answer to the realm.”
translations.idiomatic: After the armies were defeated Tuozhou realized Su Shidan had misled him. One evening he invited Bi to drink; as the wine flowed they spoke of Shidan, and Bi gently probed Tuozhou’s mood, then said forcefully, “Shidan abused power and brought you slander—only by banishing him can you answer to the realm.”

sentences.zh: 師旦坐貶官。

translations.literal: Shidan was punished by demotion.
translations.idiomatic: Shidan was demoted and banished.

sentences.zh: 璧又言：「郭倬、李汝翼僨軍誤國之罪，宜誅之以謝淮民。」

translations.literal: Bi also said: “Guo Chun and Li Ruyi, for scattering the army and misleading the state, should be executed to answer to the Huai people.”
translations.idiomatic: Bi also said, “Guo Chun and Li Ruyi scattered the army and misled the state—they should be executed to answer to the people of Huai.”

sentences.zh: 拜參知政事。

translations.literal: He was appointed participant in governance.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed participant in governance.

sentences.zh: 金遣使來，微示欲和意，丘崈以聞，璧貽崈書，俾遣小使致書金帥求成，金帥報書以用兵首謀指侂胄，侂胄大恚，不復以和為意。

translations.literal: Jin sent envoys who subtly showed a wish for peace; Qiu Chong reported this; Bi sent Chong a letter, causing him to dispatch a minor envoy to deliver a letter to the Jin commander seeking settlement; the Jin commander replied that the chief plotter in using troops was Tuozhou; Tuozhou was greatly enraged and no longer thought of peace.
translations.idiomatic: Jin sent envoys hinting at peace. Qiu Chong reported this, and Bi wrote urging him to send a minor envoy to the Jin commander to seek terms. The Jin reply named Tuozhou as the chief plotter of the war. Tuozhou was furious and abandoned any thought of peace.

sentences.zh: 璧言：「張浚以討賊復仇為己任，隆興之初，事勢未集，亦權宜就和。

translations.literal: Bi said: “Zhang Jun took punishing the enemy and avenging the feud as his own charge; at the beginning of the Longxing reign, when affairs were not yet gathered, he also expediently made peace.
translations.idiomatic: Bi said, “Zhang Jun made punishing the enemy and avenging the feud his mission; at the start of the Longxing reign, when circumstances were not yet ripe, he too made peace as an expedient.

sentences.zh: 苟利社稷，固難執一。」

translations.literal: If it profits the altars of state, it is indeed hard to hold to one course alone.”
translations.idiomatic: When the altars of state benefit, it is hard to cling to a single course.”

sentences.zh: 侂胄不聽，以張巖代崈，璧力爭，言丘崈素有人望，侂胄變色曰：「方今天下獨有一丘崈邪！」

translations.literal: Tuozhou did not listen and replaced Chong with Zhang Yan; Bi strove in argument, saying Qiu Chong had long enjoyed public esteem; Tuozhou changed color and said: “Is there only one Qiu Chong under Heaven today!”
translations.idiomatic: Tuozhou would not listen and replaced Chong with Zhang Yan. Bi argued fiercely that Qiu Chong enjoyed long-standing public esteem. Tuozhou flushed and said, “Is Qiu Chong the only man in the realm!”

sentences.zh: 吳曦叛，據蜀稱王，楊巨源、安丙誅之。

translations.literal: Wu Xi rebelled, held Sichuan and declared himself king; Yang Juyuan and An Bing executed him.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Xi rebelled, seized Sichuan, and declared himself king; Yang Juyuan and An Bing killed him.

sentences.zh: 事聞，璧議須用重臣宣撫，薦制置使楊輔為宣撫使，而使安丙輔之。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, Bi held that a weighty minister must be used as pacification commissioner; he recommended the military commissioner Yang Fu as pacification commissioner and An Bing to assist him.
translations.idiomatic: When word arrived, Bi argued that a senior minister must be sent as pacification commissioner and recommended military commissioner Yang Fu, with An Bing as his deputy.

sentences.zh: 丙殺楊巨源，輔恐召變，以書舉劉甲自代，侂胄疑輔避事，璧曰：「孝宗聞吳璘病，亟詔汪應辰權宣撫使職事，蜀賴以安，此故事也。」

translations.literal: Bing killed Yang Juyuan; Fu, fearing that summoning him would provoke change, by letter recommended Liu Jia to replace himself; Tuozhou suspected Fu of shirking affairs; Bi said: “When Emperor Xiaozong heard that Wu Lin was ill, he urgently ordered Wang Yingchen to act as pacification commissioner in charge of affairs, and Sichuan relied on this to be secure—this is an established precedent.”
translations.idiomatic: An Bing killed Yang Juyuan; Fu, fearing upheaval if recalled, recommended Liu Jia to replace him. Tuozhou suspected Fu of shirking duty. Bi said, “When Xiaozong heard Wu Lin was ill, he urgently ordered Wang Yingchen to act as pacification commissioner and Sichuan was stabilized—that is established precedent.”

sentences.zh: 於是命甲權宣撫使。

translations.literal: Thereupon Jia was ordered to act as pacification commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jia was then ordered to act as pacification commissioner.

sentences.zh: 方信孺使北歸，言金人欲縛送侂胄，故侂胄忿甚，用兵之意益急。

translations.literal: Fang Xinru returned from mission north and said the Jin people wished to bind and deliver Tuozhou; therefore Tuozhou was greatly resentful and his intent to use troops grew ever more urgent.
translations.idiomatic: When Fang Xinru returned from the north he reported that the Jin intended to bind and hand over Han Tuozhou. Tuozhou was furious and his zeal for war grew sharper still.

sentences.zh: 璧方與共政，或勸其速去，毋與侂胄分禍，璧曰：「嘻，國病矣，我去誰適謀此？」

translations.literal: Bi was then sharing in government; some urged him to leave quickly and not share calamity with Tuozhou; Bi said: “Alas, the state is ill—if I go, who is fit to plan for this?”
translations.idiomatic: While Bi was still in office, some urged him to withdraw quickly and not share Han Tuozhou’s downfall. Bi said, “Alas—the state is sick. If I leave, who is fit to handle this?”

sentences.zh: 會禮部侍郎史彌遠謀誅侂胄，以密旨告璧及錢象祖，象祖欲奏審，璧言事留恐泄，侂胄迄誅，璧兼同知樞密院事。

translations.literal: It happened that Vice Minister of Rites Shi Miyuan plotted to execute Tuozhou and informed Bi and Qian Xiangzu by secret edict; Xiangzu wished to memorialize for approval, but Bi said that delaying the matter might leak it; Tuozhou was ultimately executed, and Bi was concurrently made associate commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Vice Minister of Rites Shi Miyuan plotted to kill Tuozhou and confided the secret edict to Bi and Qian Xiangzu. Xiangzu wanted to memorialize for approval, but Bi warned that delay might leak the plan. Tuozhou was executed, and Bi was made associate commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 御史葉時論璧反復詭譎，削三秩，謫居撫州。

translations.literal: The investigating censor Ye Shi criticized Bi as changeable and deceitful; three ranks were stripped and he was banished to reside in Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Investigating censor Ye Shi attacked Bi as fickle and deceitful. Three ranks were stripped and he was banished to Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 後輔臣言誅侂胄事，璧實預聞，乃令自便。

translations.literal: Later the chief ministers spoke of the affair of executing Tuozhou; Bi had in fact been forewarned, and he was therefore allowed to act as he pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when chief ministers discussed Tuozhou’s execution, it emerged that Bi had been in on the plot, and he was allowed to go free.

sentences.zh: 復官提舉洞霄宮，久之，復以御史奏削三秩，罷祠。

translations.literal: His office was restored and he was made director of the Palace of Grotto Heaven; after a long while, again on a censor’s memorial three ranks were stripped and his sinecure ended.
translations.idiomatic: His rank was restored and he was made director of the Palace of Grotto Heaven, but years later a censor’s memorial again stripped three ranks and ended his sinecure.

sentences.zh: 越四年，復除端明殿學士、知遂寧府，未至，而潰兵張福入益昌，戕王人，略閬剽果，至遂寧，璧傳檄諭之，福等讀檄泣下，約解甲降。

translations.literal: Four years later he was again appointed academician of the Hall of Bright Clarity and prefect of Suining; before he arrived, routed troops under Zhang Fu entered Yichang, killed the king’s men, raided Lang and plundered Guo, and reached Suining; Bi issued a proclamation to instruct them; Fu and others read the proclamation and wept, agreeing to lay down arms and surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Four years later he was again made academician of the Hall of Bright Clarity and prefect of Suining. Before he arrived, mutinous troops under Zhang Fu entered Yichang, killed officials, raided Langzhou and plundered Guozhou, and reached Suining. Bi issued a proclamation; Fu and his men wept when they read it and agreed to disarm and surrender.

sentences.zh: 會官軍至挑賊，賊忿，盡燔其城，顧府治曰：「李公旦夕來居，此其勿毀。」

translations.literal: When government troops arrived and provoked the bandits, the bandits in anger burned the whole city, but looking at the prefectural seat they said: “Lord Li will come to dwell here any day—this must not be destroyed.”
translations.idiomatic: When government troops arrived and provoked them, the rebels in fury burned the whole city but spared the prefectural compound, saying, “Lord Li will arrive any day—do not destroy this.”

sentences.zh: 璧馳書大將張威，使調嘉定黎雅砦丁、牌手來會戰，威夜遣人叩門，來言曰：「賊壘堅不可破，將選死士，梯而登，以火攻之。」

translations.literal: Bi sent a urgent letter to the great general Zhang Wei, causing him to mobilize the stockaded militia and archers of Jiading and Liya for a joint battle; Wei at night sent a man to knock at the gate and came to say: “The bandits’ stockade is firm and cannot be broken; we will select dare-to-die men, scale by ladder, and attack with fire.”
translations.idiomatic: Bi urgently wrote the general Zhang Wei to mobilize militia and archers from the Jiading and Liya stockades. Wei sent a messenger at night who said, “The rebel stockade is too strong to storm. We will pick dare-to-die men, scale the walls, and burn them out.”

sentences.zh: 璧曰：「審爾，必多殺士卒，盍先斷賊汲路與糧道，使不得食，即自成擒矣。」

translations.literal: Bi said: “If it is truly so, many soldiers will surely be killed—why not first cut off the bandits’ water route and grain route so they cannot eat, and they will be captured of themselves?”
translations.idiomatic: Bi said, “If you do that, many soldiers will die. Better first cut their water and grain routes so they starve—they will surrender themselves.”

sentences.zh: 以長圍法授之，威用其謀，賊遂平。

translations.literal: He taught him the method of long encirclement; Wei used his plan and the bandits were thereupon pacified.
translations.idiomatic: He taught Wei the method of prolonged encirclement. Wei followed his plan and the rebels were pacified.

sentences.zh: 璧尋引疾奉祠。

translations.literal: Bi soon cited illness and received a sinecure.
translations.idiomatic: Bi soon pleaded illness and took a sinecure post.

sentences.zh: 嘉定十五年六月卒，進資政殿學士致仕，諡「文懿」。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the fifteenth year of Jiading he died; he was advanced to academician of the Hall of Government Affairs in retirement, with the posthumous title “Cultured and Excellent.”
translations.idiomatic: He died in the sixth month of Jiading 15, having been advanced to academician of the Hall of Government Affairs in retirement, with the posthumous title Cultured and Excellent.

sentences.zh: 璧嗜學如饑渴，群經百氏搜抉靡遺，于典章制度尤綜練。

translations.literal: Bi loved learning like hunger and thirst; among the classics and the hundred schools he searched and selected without omission, and in statutes and institutions he was especially comprehensive and practiced.
translations.idiomatic: Bi hungered for learning, combing the classics and the hundred schools without omission, and was especially masterful in statutes and institutions.

sentences.zh: 為文雋逸，所著有《雁湖集》一百卷、《涓塵錄》三卷、《中興戰功錄》三卷、《中興奏議》若干卷、內外制二十卷、《援毫錄》八十卷、《臨汝閒書》百五十卷。

translations.literal: His writing was elegant and lofty; works he authored include Collected Works from Goose Lake in one hundred juan, Record of Dust in three juan, Record of Military Achievements in the Restoration in three juan, Memorials of the Restoration in several juan, Inner and Outer Drafts in twenty juan, Record of Brush-Holding in eighty juan, and Leisure Writings from Linru in one hundred fifty juan.
translations.idiomatic: His prose was elegant and elevated. His works included Collected Works from Goose Lake (100 juan), Record of Dust (3 juan), Record of Military Achievements in the Restoration (3 juan), Memorials of the Restoration (several juan), Inner and Outer Drafts (20 juan), Record of Brush-Holding (80 juan), and Leisure Writings from Linru (150 juan).

sentences.zh: 璧父子與弟𡌴皆以文學知名，蜀人比之三蘇雲。

translations.literal: Bi, his father and son, and his younger brother Sao were all renowned for literary learning; people of Shu compared them to the three Sus, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: Bi, his father and son, and his younger brother Sao were all famed for letters; Sichuan folk likened them to the three Sus of old.

sentences.zh: 丘崈，字宗卿，江陰軍人。

translations.literal: Qiu Chong, courtesy name Zongqing, was a native of Jiangyin Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu Chong, whose courtesy name was Zongqing, came from Jiangyin Circuit.

sentences.zh: 隆興元年進士，為建康府觀察推官。

translations.literal: A jinshi of the first year of Longxing, he served as investigating clerk of Jiankang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: A jinshi of Longxing 1, he served as investigating clerk in Jiankang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 丞相虞允文奇其才，奏除國子博士。

translations.literal: Chief councilor Yu Yunwen marveled at his talent and memorialized to appoint him erudite of the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Councilor Yu Yunwen admired his talent and had him appointed erudite of the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 孝宗諭允文舉自代者，允文首薦崈。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaozong instructed Yunwen to recommend someone to replace himself; Yunwen first recommended Chong.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaozong asked Yunwen to recommend his successor, Yunwen named Chong first.

sentences.zh: 有旨賜對，遂言：「恢復之志不可忘，恢復之事未易舉，宜甄拔實才，責以內治，遵養十年，乃可議北向。」

translations.literal: There was an edict granting him audience; he thereupon said: “The will to recover cannot be forgotten, but the undertaking of recovery is not easy to raise; one should select and promote men of real talent, charge them with internal governance, nurture the realm for ten years, and only then may one discuss turning north.
translations.idiomatic: Summoned to audience, he said, “The will to recover the north must never be forgotten, but recovery is not easily undertaken. Select true talent, charge them with internal governance, nurture the realm for ten years, and only then discuss marching north.”

sentences.zh: 時方遣范成大使金，祈請陵寢。

translations.literal: At that time Fan Chengda was being dispatched as envoy to Jin to pray for the imperial tombs.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Chengda was then being sent as envoy to Jin to petition for access to the imperial tombs.

sentences.zh: 崈言：「泛使亟遣，無益大計，徒以驕敵。」

translations.literal: Chong said: “General envoys sent in haste benefit not the great plan and only make the enemy arrogant.”
translations.idiomatic: Chong said, “Sending general envoys in haste does nothing for the grand strategy—it only emboldens the enemy.”

sentences.zh: 孝宗不樂，曰：「卿家墳墓為人所據，亦須理索否？」

translations.literal: Xiaozong was displeased and said: “Your family’s graves are occupied by others—must they not also be pursued and reclaimed?”
translations.idiomatic: Xiaozong was displeased and said, “If your family graves were seized by others, would you not demand them back?”

sentences.zh: 崈對曰：「臣但能訴之，不能請之。」

translations.literal: Chong replied: “Your servant can only lodge complaint, not request them back.”
translations.idiomatic: Chong replied, “I could lodge a complaint, but I could not demand their return.”

sentences.zh: 孝宗怒，崈退待罪，孝宗察其忠，不譴也。

translations.literal: Xiaozong was angry; Chong withdrew to await punishment; Xiaozong perceived his loyalty and did not reprove him.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaozong was angry; Chong withdrew to await punishment, but Xiaozong saw his loyalty and did not punish him.

sentences.zh: 遷太常博士，出知秀州華亭縣。

translations.literal: He was transferred to erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and went out as magistrate of Huating County in Xiuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and sent out as magistrate of Huating County in Xiuzhou.

sentences.zh: 捍海堰廢且百年，鹹潮歲大入，壞並海田，蘇、湖皆被其害。

translations.literal: The sea-bank dyke had been abandoned for nearly a century; salt tides each year entered greatly, ruining fields along the sea, and Su and Hu were both harmed.
translations.idiomatic: The coastal sea-wall dyke had lain in ruins for nearly a century; salt tides flooded in yearly, destroying seaside fields and harming both Suzhou and Huzhou.

sentences.zh: 崈至海口，訪遺址已淪沒，乃奏創築，三月堰成，三州舄鹵復為良田。

translations.literal: Chong reached the estuary, sought the old site already submerged, and memorialized to build anew; in three months the dyke was completed and the saline fields of the three prefectures again became fertile farmland.
translations.idiomatic: Chong went to the estuary, found the old site submerged, and memorialized to rebuild the dyke. In three months it was finished and the saline fields of three prefectures became fertile farmland again.

sentences.zh: 除直秘閣、知平江府，入奏內殿，因論楮幣折閱，請公私出內，並以錢會各半為定法。

translations.literal: He was appointed to the Direct Secretariat and made prefect of Pingjiang; entering to memorialize in the inner hall, he discussed the depreciation of paper currency and requested that public and private outlays from the inner treasury be fixed by law as half cash notes and half coin.
translations.idiomatic: Appointed to the Direct Secretariat and made prefect of Pingjiang, he memorialized in the inner hall on paper-currency depreciation and proposed that public and private payments from the inner treasury be fixed by law at half cash notes and half coin.

sentences.zh: 詔行其言，天下便之。

translations.literal: An edict carried out his words and the realm found it convenient.
translations.idiomatic: An edict adopted his proposal, to the realm’s relief.

sentences.zh: 知吉州，召除戶部郎中，遷樞密院檢詳文字。

translations.literal: He governed Jizhou, was summoned and appointed director in the Ministry of Revenue, and was transferred to textual reviewer at the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: As prefect of Jizhou he was recalled, appointed director in the Ministry of Revenue, and transferred to textual reviewer at the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 被命接伴金國賀生辰使。

translations.literal: He received orders to receive and accompany the Jin envoys congratulating the birthday.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered to receive and accompany the Jin envoys sent for the imperial birthday.

sentences.zh: 金曆九月晦，與《統天曆》不合，崈接使者以恩意，乃徐告以南北曆法異同，合從會慶節正日隨班上壽。

translations.literal: The Jin calendar’s last day of the ninth month did not agree with the Tongtian Calendar; Chong received the envoys with gracious intent and then slowly informed them of the differences between northern and southern calendrical methods, that they should follow the proper day of the Festival of Joint Celebration and offer birthday felicitations with the court on schedule.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin calendar’s last day of the ninth month disagreed with the Tongtian Calendar. Chong received the envoys graciously, then explained the calendrical differences and directed them to offer birthday felicitations on the proper day of the Festival of Joint Celebration with the court.

sentences.zh: 金使初難之，卒屈服。

translations.literal: The Jin envoys at first resisted, but in the end submitted.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin envoys resisted at first but ultimately yielded.

sentences.zh: 孝宗喜謂崈曰：「使人聽命成禮而還，卿之力也。」

translations.literal: Xiaozong said with pleasure to Chong: “The envoys obeyed orders, completed the rites, and returned—this is your strength.”
translations.idiomatic: Xiaozong said with pleasure, “The envoys obeyed and completed the rites and returned—that was your doing.”

sentences.zh: 先是，王抃為樞密，崈不少下之。

translations.literal: Earlier Wang Bian was military commissioner and Chong would not yield to him in the least.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Wang Bian was military commissioner, and Chong would not defer to him.

sentences.zh: 方迓客時，抃排定程頓奏，上降付接伴，令沿途遵執。

translations.literal: Just as he was receiving guests, Bian arranged a fixed itinerary and presented a memorial; the emperor transmitted it to the receiving officer with orders to follow it along the route.
translations.idiomatic: As Chong was receiving the envoys, Bian drew up a fixed itinerary and memorialized it; the emperor transmitted it to the receiving officer with orders to follow it along the route.

sentences.zh: 崈具奏，謂「不可以此啟敵疑心。」

translations.literal: Chong fully memorialized, saying: “One cannot by this arouse the enemy’s suspicions.”
translations.idiomatic: Chong memorialized in full, saying, “This must not be used to arouse the enemy’s suspicions.”

sentences.zh: 不奉詔。

translations.literal: He did not obey the edict.
translations.idiomatic: He refused to obey the edict.

sentences.zh: 抃憾之，訾崈不禮金使，予祠。

translations.literal: Bian resented this and slandered Chong for discourtesy to the Jin envoys; he was given a sinecure.
translations.idiomatic: Bian resented this and accused Chong of discourtesy to the Jin envoys; Chong was given a sinecure post.

sentences.zh: 起知鄂州，移江西轉運判官，提點浙東刑獄，進直徽猷閣、知平江府，升龍圖閣，移帥紹興府，改兩浙轉運副使，以憂去。

translations.literal: He was raised to govern Ezhou, transferred as transport judge of Jiangxi, made judicial intendant of eastern Zhejiang, advanced to the Direct Huaiyou Pavilion and prefect of Pingjiang, promoted to the Dragon Diagram Pavilion, transferred to command Shaoxing, changed to vice transport commissioner of the two Zhe, and left on account of mourning.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to govern Ezhou, served as transport judge of Jiangxi and judicial intendant of eastern Zhejiang, was advanced to the Direct Huaiyou Pavilion and prefect of Pingjiang, promoted to the Dragon Diagram Pavilion, commanded Shaoxing, became vice transport commissioner of the two Zhe, and left on mourning leave.

sentences.zh: 光宗即位，召對，除太常少卿兼權工部侍郎，進戶部侍郎，擢煥章閣直學士、四川安撫制置使兼知成都府。

translations.literal: When Emperor Guangzong ascended, he was summoned for audience, appointed vice minister of imperial sacrifices and concurrently acting vice minister of works, advanced to vice minister of revenue, and promoted to academician of the Huanzhang Pavilion, Sichuan pacification and military commissioner concurrently prefect of Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: When Guangzong ascended, Chong was summoned, appointed vice minister of imperial sacrifices and acting vice minister of works, promoted to vice minister of revenue, and made academician of the Huanzhang Pavilion, Sichuan pacification commissioner, and concurrently prefect of Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 崈素以吳氏世掌兵為慮，陛辭，奏曰：「臣入蜀後，吳挺脫至死亡，兵權不可復付其子。

translations.literal: Chong had long been concerned that the Wu clan held the armies for generations; at his farewell audience he memorialized: “After your servant enters Shu, when Wu Ting comes to die, military authority must not again be given to his son.
translations.idiomatic: Chong had long worried that the Wu clan held military power for generations. At his farewell audience he said, “After I enter Shu, when Wu Ting dies, military authority must not pass to his son again.

sentences.zh: 臣請得便宜撫定諸軍，以俟朝命。」

translations.literal: Your servant requests leave to act expediently in pacifying and settling the armies, to await court orders.”
translations.idiomatic: I ask leave to act expediently in settling the armies until the court decides.”

sentences.zh: 挺死，崈即奏：「乞選他將代之，仍置副帥，別差興州守臣，並利州西路帥司歸興元，以殺其權。

translations.literal: When Ting died, Chong immediately memorialized: “I beg to select another general to replace him, still set up a deputy commander, separately assign the Xingzhou prefect, and return the Western Circuit of Lizhou command to Xingyuan, to diminish their power.
translations.idiomatic: When Ting died, Chong immediately memorialized, “Select another general to replace him, appoint a deputy commander, assign a separate Xingzhou prefect, and return the Western Circuit of Lizhou command to Xingyuan to curb their power.

sentences.zh: 挺長子曦勿令奔喪，起復知和州，屬總領楊輔就近節制諸軍，檄利路提刑楊虞仲往攝興州。」

translations.literal: Do not let Ting’s eldest son Xi go to mourn; recall him to active service as prefect of Hezhou; entrust the overall commander Yang Fu to regulate the armies nearby; order Lizhou judicial intendant Yang Yuzhong to go and act as Xingzhou.”
translations.idiomatic: Do not let Ting’s eldest son Xi return for mourning; recall him to govern Hezhou; place overall commander Yang Fu nearby to regulate the armies; and send Lizhou judicial intendant Yang Yuzhong to act as Xingzhou commander.”

sentences.zh: 朝廷命張詔代挺，以李仁廣副之，遂革世將之患。

translations.literal: The court appointed Zhang Zhao to replace Ting, with Li Renguang as deputy, and thereby reformed the trouble of hereditary commanders.
translations.idiomatic: The court appointed Zhang Zhao to replace Ting with Li Renguang as deputy, ending the hereditary-commander problem.

sentences.zh: 其後郭杲繼詔復兼利西路安撫。

translations.literal: Afterward Guo Gao succeeded Zhao and again concurrently held the Western Circuit of Lizhou pacification commission.
translations.idiomatic: Later Guo Gao succeeded Zhao and again held the Western Circuit of Lizhou pacification commission.

sentences.zh: 杲死，韓侂胄復以兵權付曦，曦叛，識者乃服崈先見。

translations.literal: When Gao died, Han Tuozhou again gave military authority to Xi; Xi rebelled, and those who knew admitted Chong’s foresight.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao died, Han Tuozhou again gave military power to Xi; Xi rebelled, and observers then acknowledged Chong’s foresight.

sentences.zh: 進煥章閣直學士。

translations.literal: He was advanced to academician of the Huanzhang Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: He was advanced to academician of the Huanzhang Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 寧宗即位，赴召，以中丞謝深甫論罷之。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ningzong ascended, he answered the summons but was dismissed on the censor-in-chief Xie Shenfu’s criticism.
translations.idiomatic: When Ningzong ascended, he answered the summons but was dismissed on Censor-in-Chief Xie Shenfu’s memorial.

sentences.zh: 居數年，復職知慶元府。

translations.literal: After several years he was restored to office as prefect of Qingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Several years later he was restored and made prefect of Qingyuan.

sentences.zh: 既入奏，韓侂胄招以見，出奏疏幾二千言示崈，蓋北伐議也，知崈平日主復仇，冀可與共功名。

translations.literal: After entering to memorialize, Han Tuozhou summoned him to an audience and produced a memorial of nearly two thousand words to show Chong—it was a plan for northern expedition; knowing that Chong ordinarily advocated avenging the feud, he hoped they could share merit together.
translations.idiomatic: After his audience memorial, Han Tuozhou summoned him and showed him a nearly two-thousand-word memorial for a northern expedition, knowing Chong had long favored vengeance and hoping to win him as an ally.

sentences.zh: 崈曰：「中原淪陷且百年，在我固不可一日而忘也，然兵凶戰危，若首倡非常之舉，兵交勝負未可知，則首事之禍，其誰任之？

translations.literal: Chong said: “The Central Plains have been lost for nearly a century; for us it indeed cannot be forgotten for a single day, yet arms are inauspicious and war perilous—if one first raises an extraordinary undertaking and when armies clash victory and defeat are unknown, then the calamity of being first to act—who will bear it?
translations.idiomatic: Chong said, “The Central Plains have been lost for nearly a century—we must never forget that for a day. Yet war is perilous. If you launch an extraordinary campaign and victory is uncertain, who will bear the blame for being first to act?

sentences.zh: 此必有誇誕貪進之人，攘臂以僥倖萬一，宜亟斥絕，不然必誤國矣。」

translations.literal: There will surely be boastful, reckless, greedy men who roll up their sleeves to gamble on a one-in-ten-thousand chance—you should quickly reject and cut them off, or else you will surely mislead the state.”
translations.idiomatic: Boastful, reckless men will roll up their sleeves to gamble on a slim chance. Reject them at once, or you will ruin the state.”

sentences.zh: 進敷文閣學士，改知建康府。

translations.literal: He was advanced to academician of the Hall for Spreading Culture and changed to prefect of Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: He was advanced to academician of the Hall for Spreading Culture and made prefect of Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 將行，侂胄曰：「此事姑為遲之。」

translations.literal: As he was about to depart, Tuozhou said: “This matter for now let it be delayed.”
translations.idiomatic: As he was about to leave, Tuozhou said, “Let us delay this matter for now.”

sentences.zh: 崈因贊曰：「翻然而改，誠社稷生靈之幸，惟無搖於異議，則善矣。」

translations.literal: Chong thereupon praised him: “To turn and change is truly the fortune of the altars and the people—only do not waver at dissenting views, and it will be good.”
translations.idiomatic: Chong praised him, “To change course would be the realm’s good fortune—only do not waver at dissent, and all will be well.”

sentences.zh: 侂胄聞金人置平章，宣撫河南，奏以崈為簽樞，宣撫江、淮以應之。

translations.literal: Tuozhou heard that the Jin had set up a chief councilor and pacification commissioner for Henan, and memorialized to make Chong deputy military commissioner and pacification commissioner for the Yangzi and Huai to meet them.
translations.idiomatic: Tuozhou heard the Jin had appointed a chief councilor and Henan pacification commissioner and memorialized to make Chong deputy military commissioner and Yangzi-Huai pacification commissioner in response.

sentences.zh: 崈手書力論「金人未必有意敗盟，中國當示大體，宜申警軍實，使吾常有勝勢。

translations.literal: Chong by hand wrote forcefully arguing: “The Jin people may not necessarily intend to break the alliance; China should display the great framework; one should proclaim and warn of military readiness so that we always have a posture of victory.
translations.idiomatic: Chong wrote forcefully, “The Jin may not intend to break the alliance. China should show magnanimity, strengthen military readiness, and keep ourselves in a position to win.

sentences.zh: 若釁自彼作，我有辭矣。」

translations.literal: If provocation comes from them, we have justification.”
translations.idiomatic: If they provoke war, we will be in the right.”

sentences.zh: 宣撫議遂寢。

translations.literal: The pacification commission plan was thereupon shelved.
translations.idiomatic: The pacification commission plan was shelved.

sentences.zh: 侂胄移書欲除崈內職，宣諭兩淮。

translations.literal: Tuozhou sent a letter wishing to appoint Chong to an inner-court post to proclaim instructions to the two Huai circuits.
translations.idiomatic: Tuozhou wrote wishing to give Chong an inner-court post to proclaim instructions to the two Huai circuits.

sentences.zh: 崈報曰：「使名雖異，其為示敵人以嫌疑之跡則同，且偽平章宣撫既寢，尤不宜輕舉。」

translations.literal: Chong replied: “Though the envoy’s title differs, in showing the enemy traces of suspicion it is the same; moreover, since the false chief councilor and pacification commission has been shelved, it is especially unsuitable to act lightly.”
translations.idiomatic: Chong replied, “Though the title differs, it still shows the enemy grounds for suspicion. Since the Jin pacification post is already shelved, we especially should not act rashly.”

sentences.zh: 侂胄滋不悅。

translations.literal: Tuozhou grew ever more displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Tuozhou grew more displeased.

sentences.zh: 升寶文閣學士、刑部尚書、江淮宣撫使。

translations.literal: He was promoted to academician of the Hall for Treasuring Culture, minister of justice, and Yangzi-Huai pacification commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to academician of the Hall for Treasuring Culture, minister of justice, and Yangzi-Huai pacification commissioner.

sentences.zh: 時宋師克泗州，進圖宿、壽，既而師潰，侂胄遣人來議招收潰卒，且求自解之計。

translations.literal: At that time Song armies captured Sizhou and advanced to besiege Suzhou and Shouzhou; soon after the armies collapsed; Tuozhou sent men to discuss gathering the routed troops and also sought a plan for his own vindication.
translations.idiomatic: Song forces had captured Sizhou and advanced on Suzhou and Shouzhou, then collapsed. Tuozhou sent men to discuss gathering routed troops and to seek a way to clear himself.

sentences.zh: 崈謂：「宜明蘇師旦、周筠等僨師之姦，正李汝翼、郭倬等喪師之罪。」

translations.literal: Chong said: “One should clarify the treachery of Su Shidan, Zhou Yun, and others in scattering the army, and rectify the crime of Li Ruyi, Guo Chun, and others in losing the army.”
translations.idiomatic: Chong said, “Expose the treachery of Su Shidan, Zhou Yun, and others who scattered the army, and punish Li Ruyi, Guo Chun, and others who lost it.”

sentences.zh: 崈欲全淮東兵力，為兩淮聲援，奏「泗州孤立，淮北所屯精兵幾二萬，萬一金人南出清河口及犯天長等城，則首尾中斷，墮敵計矣。

translations.literal: Chong wished to preserve Huaidong’s military strength as support for the two Huai, and memorialized: “Sizhou stands isolated; nearly twenty thousand elite troops are stationed north of the Huai—if by any chance the Jin go south from Qinghekou and attack Tiancheng and other cities, then head and tail will be cut off and we will fall into the enemy’s plan.
translations.idiomatic: Wishing to preserve Huaidong strength as support for both Huai circuits, he memorialized, “Sizhou stands isolated with nearly twenty thousand elite troops north of the Huai. If the Jin strike south from Qinghekou or attack Tiancheng, our forces will be cut off and fall into their trap.

sentences.zh: 莫若棄之，還軍盱眙。」

translations.literal: Better to abandon it and return the army to Xuyi.”
translations.idiomatic: Better abandon it and withdraw the army to Xuyi.”

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: This was followed.
translations.idiomatic: His advice was followed.

sentences.zh: 金人擁眾自渦口犯淮南，或勸崈棄廬、和州為守江計，崈曰：「棄淮則與敵共長江之險矣。

translations.literal: The Jin mustered a host from Wokou and invaded Huainan; some urged Chong to abandon Luzhou and Hezhou as a plan to defend the Yangzi; Chong said: “To abandon the Huai is to share the Yangzi’s peril with the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Jin forces massed at Wokou and invaded Huainan. Some urged Chong to abandon Luzhou and Hezhou to defend the Yangzi. Chong said, “Abandon the Huai and we share the Yangzi’s defenses with the enemy.

sentences.zh: 吾當與淮南俱存亡。」

translations.literal: I shall live and die together with Huainan.”
translations.idiomatic: I will live or die with Huainan.”

sentences.zh: 益增兵為防。

translations.literal: He further increased troops for defense.
translations.idiomatic: He reinforced the garrisons.

sentences.zh: 進端明殿學士、侍讀，尋拜簽書樞密院，督視江、淮軍馬。

translations.literal: He was advanced to academician of the Hall of Bright Clarity and reader-in-waiting, and soon appointed deputy to the Bureau of Military Affairs to supervise Jiang and Huai military forces.
translations.idiomatic: He was advanced to academician of the Hall of Bright Clarity and reader-in-waiting, then appointed deputy military commissioner to supervise Jiang and Huai forces.

sentences.zh: 有自北來者韓元靖，自謂琦五世孫，崈詰所以來之故，元靖言：「兩國交兵，北朝皆謂出韓太師意，今相州宗族墳墓皆不可保，故來依太師爾。」

translations.literal: There came from the north Han Yuanjing, who called himself the fifth-generation descendant of Han Qi; Chong interrogated the reason for his coming; Yuanjing said: “The two states are at war; the northern court all say it proceeds from Grand Mentor Han’s intent; now the clan graves at Xiangzhou cannot be preserved—therefore I come to rely on the Grand Mentor.”
translations.idiomatic: Han Yuanjing came from the north claiming to be Han Qi’s fifth-generation descendant. Chong questioned his purpose. Yuanjing said, “Both courts are at war; the north says it is Grand Mentor Han’s doing. Our clan graves at Xiangzhou are no longer safe, so I have come to rely on the Grand Mentor.”

sentences.zh: 崈使畢其說，始露講解意。

translations.literal: Chong had him finish his speech, and he then revealed an intent to discuss settlement.
translations.idiomatic: Chong let him finish, and he then revealed a wish to discuss peace.

sentences.zh: 崈遣人護送北歸，俾扣其實。

translations.literal: Chong sent men to escort him back north and caused him to probe the truth.
translations.idiomatic: Chong sent escorts to return him north and probe the truth.

sentences.zh: 其回也，得金行省幅紙，崈以聞於朝，遂遣王文采持書幣以行。

translations.literal: On his return he obtained a sheet from the Jin Branch Secretariat; Chong reported it to court, and thereupon Wang Wencai was dispatched bearing letters and gifts.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he brought a note from the Jin Branch Secretariat. Chong reported it to court, and Wang Wencai was sent with letters and gifts.

sentences.zh: 文采還，金帥答書辭順，崈復以聞，遂遣陳璧充小使。

translations.literal: Wencai returned; the Jin commander’s reply was conciliatory in wording; Chong again reported it, and Chen Bi was sent as minor envoy.
translations.idiomatic: Wencai returned with a conciliatory reply from the Jin commander. Chong reported again, and Chen Bi was sent as minor envoy.

sentences.zh: 璧回，具言：「金人詰使介，既欲和矣，何為出兵真州以襲我？

translations.literal: Bi returned and fully stated: “The Jin people questioned the envoy’s credentials: since you wish peace, why send troops from Zhenzhou to attack us?
translations.idiomatic: Bi returned reporting, “The Jin questioned our envoy: if you want peace, why did troops from Zhenzhou attack us?

sentences.zh: 然仍露和意也。」

translations.literal: Yet they still revealed an intent for peace.”
translations.idiomatic: Yet they still showed a desire for peace.”

sentences.zh: 崈白廟堂，請自朝廷移書續前議，又謂彼既指侂胄為元謀，若移書，宜暫免係銜。

translations.literal: Chong informed the chief ministers, requesting that the court itself send a letter continuing the prior discussions; he also said that since they had pointed to Tuozhou as the chief plotter, if a letter were sent, his formal title should temporarily be omitted.
translations.idiomatic: Chong told the chief ministers the court should send a letter continuing talks, and since the Jin named Tuozhou as chief plotter, his title should be omitted from the letter.

sentences.zh: 侂胄大怒，罷崈，以知樞密院事張巖代之。

translations.literal: Tuozhou was greatly enraged, dismissed Chong, and replaced him with Zhang Yan, who knew the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Tuozhou was furious, dismissed Chong, and replaced him with Zhang Yan, commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 既以臺論，提舉洞霄宮，落職。

translations.literal: Then on censorial criticism he was made director of the Palace of Grotto Heaven and stripped of office.
translations.idiomatic: Censors then attacked him; he was made director of the Palace of Grotto Heaven and stripped of rank.

sentences.zh: 侂胄誅，以資政殿學士知建康府，尋改江、淮制置大使兼知建康府。

translations.literal: After Tuozhou was executed, he was made academician of the Hall of Government Affairs and prefect of Jiankang; soon changed to great commissioner for Jiang-Huai pacification concurrently prefect of Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: After Tuozhou was executed, he was made academician of the Hall of Government Affairs and prefect of Jiankang, soon becoming great Jiang-Huai pacification commissioner while retaining the Jiankang prefecture.

sentences.zh: 淮南運司招輯邊民二萬，號「雄淮軍」，月廩不繼，公肆剽劫，崈乃隨「雄淮」所屯，分隸守臣節制，其西路則同轉運使張穎揀刺為御前武定軍，以三萬人為額，分為六軍，餘汰歸農，自是月省錢二十八萬緡，米三萬四千石。

translations.literal: The Huainan transport office gathered twenty thousand border people called the “Valiant Huai Army”; monthly rations did not continue and they openly plundered; Chong then according to where the Valiant Huai were stationed divided them under the regulation of defending officials; on the western route he together with transport commissioner Zhang Ying selected and mustered them as the Imperial Front Martial Stability Army, with a quota of thirty thousand, divided into six armies; the remainder were culled back to farming—thereafter each month twenty-eight myriad strings of cash and thirty-four thousand shi of grain were saved.
translations.idiomatic: The Huainan transport office had gathered twenty thousand border people as the “Valiant Huai Army.” When monthly rations failed they plundered openly. Chong placed them under local commanders by garrison; on the western route he and transport commissioner Zhang Ying reorganized them as the Imperial Front Martial Stability Army—thirty thousand in six divisions, the rest returned to farming—saving twenty-eight myriad strings of cash and thirty-four thousand shi of grain monthly.

sentences.zh: 武定既成軍伍，淮西賴其力。

translations.literal: Once Martial Stability was formed as an army, western Huai relied on its strength.
translations.idiomatic: Once Martial Stability was organized, western Huai relied on its strength.

sentences.zh: 以病丐歸，拜同知樞密院事。

translations.literal: Citing illness he begged to return and was appointed associate commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Pleading illness, he asked to retire and was appointed associate military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 卒，諡「忠定」。

translations.literal: He died; posthumous title “Loyal and Settled.”
translations.idiomatic: He died and was given the posthumous title Loyal and Settled.

sentences.zh: 崈儀狀魁傑，機神英悟，嘗慷慨謂人曰：「生無以報國，死願為猛將以滅敵。」

translations.literal: Chong’s bearing was towering and heroic, his wit keen and perceptive; he once said passionately to others: “In life I have no means to repay the state; in death I wish to be a fierce general to destroy the enemy.”
translations.idiomatic: Chong was tall and imposing, keen and perceptive. He once said passionately, “In life I have not repaid the state; in death I wish to be a fierce general who destroys the enemy.”

sentences.zh: 其忠義性然也。

translations.literal: Such was his loyal and righteous nature.
translations.idiomatic: Such was his loyal and righteous nature.

sentences.zh: 倪思，字正甫，湖州歸安人。

translations.literal: Ni Si, courtesy name Zhengfu, was a native of Gui’an in Huzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Ni Si, whose courtesy name was Zhengfu, came from Gui’an in Huzhou.

sentences.zh: 乾道二年進士，中博學宏詞科。

translations.literal: A jinshi of the second year of Qiandao, he passed the erudite learning and grand rhetoric examination.
translations.idiomatic: A jinshi of Qiandao 2, he also passed the erudite learning and grand rhetoric examination.

sentences.zh: 累遷秘書郎，除著作郎兼翰林權直。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to secretary; appointed compiler and concurrently acting Hanlin attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through the Secretariat to compiler and acting Hanlin attendant.

sentences.zh: 光宗即位，典冊與尤袤對掌。

translations.literal: When Emperor Guangzong ascended, he and You Mao jointly directed the ceremonial documents.
translations.idiomatic: When Guangzong ascended, he and You Mao jointly directed the ceremonial documents.

sentences.zh: 故事，行三制並宣學士。

translations.literal: By precedent, three edicts were issued and the academician announced them.
translations.idiomatic: By precedent three edicts were issued and the academician announced them.

sentences.zh: 上欲試思能否，一夕並草除公師四制，訓詞精敏，在廷誦歎。

translations.literal: The emperor wished to test whether Si was capable; in one night he together drafted four edicts appointing dukes and grand mentors; the instructions were refined and keen, and those at court recited them in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wished to test Si’s ability and in one night had him draft four edicts appointing dukes and grand mentors. The language was refined and keen, and the court marveled.

sentences.zh: 權侍立修注官，直前奏：「陛下方受禪，金主亦新立，欲制其命，必每事有以勝之，彼奢則以儉勝之，彼暴則以仁勝之，彼怠惰則以憂勤勝之。」

translations.literal: As acting attendant revision-and-annotation officer standing by, he stepped forward and memorialized: “Your Majesty has just received the abdication; the Jin ruler has also newly ascended—if you wish to control his mandate, in every matter you must have something by which to overcome him: if he is extravagant, then overcome him with frugality; if he is violent, then overcome him with benevolence; if he is idle and lazy, then overcome him with anxious diligence.”
translations.idiomatic: As acting revision officer in attendance, he stepped forward and said, “Your Majesty has just received the abdication and the Jin ruler has also newly ascended. To control his mandate, you must surpass him in every respect—meet extravagance with frugality, violence with benevolence, and idleness with anxious diligence.”

sentences.zh: 又請增置諫官，專責以諫事。

translations.literal: He also requested adding remonstrance officials charged solely with remonstrance affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He also asked to add remonstrance officials charged solely with remonstrance duties.

sentences.zh: 又乞召內外諸將訪問，以知其才否。

translations.literal: He also requested summoning generals inside and outside to inquire of them, so as to learn whether they had talent or not.
translations.idiomatic: He also asked that generals throughout the realm be summoned and questioned to assess their abilities.

sentences.zh: 遷將作少監兼權直學士院，兼權中書舍人，升中書舍人兼直學士院、同修國史，尋兼侍講。
