translations.literal: He was transferred to vice director of the Directorate of Palace Buildings, concurrently acting director of the Academy of Scholarly Worthies and concurrently acting drafter of the Secretariat; promoted to drafter of the Secretariat concurrently director of the Academy of Scholarly Worthies and associate compiler of the national history; soon after also lecturing attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was made vice director of the Directorate of Palace Buildings and acting director of the Hanlin Academy and acting Secretariat drafter, then promoted to Secretariat drafter with concurrent Hanlin Academy directorship and associate national-history compiler, and soon after added lecturer in attendance.

sentences.zh: 初，孝宗以戶部經費之餘，則於三省置封樁庫以待軍用，至紹熙移用始頻。

translations.literal: At first, Emperor Xiaozong, taking what remained of the Ministry of Revenue’s regular budget, established sealed reserve treasuries in the Three Departments to await military use; by the Shaoxi reign diversions for other purposes began to grow frequent.
translations.idiomatic: Initially Xiaozong had set aside the Ministry of Revenue’s surplus in sealed reserve treasuries across the Three Departments for military needs; under Shaoxi, raids on those funds grew ever more frequent.

sentences.zh: 會有詔發緡錢十五萬入內帑備犒軍，思謂實給他費，請毋發，且曰：「往歲所入，約四百六十四萬緡，所出之錢不及二萬，非痛加撙節，則封樁自此無儲。

translations.literal: It happened that an edict ordered one hundred fifty thousand strings of cash sent to the inner treasury to provision troop rewards; Si said it would in fact supply other expenses and requested that it not be issued, and further said: “In recent years receipts amounted to roughly four million six hundred forty thousand strings, while disbursements did not reach twenty thousand—unless strict economy is enforced, the sealed reserves will from this point have no stores.
translations.idiomatic: When an edict ordered one hundred fifty thousand strings transferred to the inner treasury for troop rewards, Si argued the money would actually cover other expenses and urged against the withdrawal, saying, “Annual receipts run to some four million six hundred forty thousand strings, yet outlays barely reach twenty thousand. Without severe austerity the sealed reserves will soon be empty.

sentences.zh: 遂定議犒軍歲以四十萬緡為額，由是費用有節。

translations.literal: Thereupon it was settled by deliberation that troop rewards each year would take four hundred thousand strings as the quota, and from this expenditures were regulated.
translations.idiomatic: The court then fixed annual troop rewards at four hundred thousand strings, and spending thereafter was kept in check.

sentences.zh: 又言：「唐制使諫官隨宰相入閣，今諫官月一對耳，乞許同宰執宣引，庶得從容論奏。」

translations.literal: He also said: “Under the Tang system remonstrance officials accompanied chief councilors into the privy chamber; today remonstrance officials have audience only once a month—I beg permission to enter together with the chief councilors for announcement and presentation, so that one may at leisure discuss and memorialize.”
translations.idiomatic: He also memorialized: “Tang practice had remonstrance officials follow chief councilors into the privy chamber, whereas today they face the throne only once a month. I ask that they be allowed to enter with the chief councilors for audience, so remonstrance can be offered at leisure.”

sentences.zh: 上稱善，除禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: The emperor praised this as good and appointed him vice minister of rites.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved and appointed him vice minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 上久不過重華宮，思疏十上，言多痛切。

translations.literal: The emperor for a long time did not visit Chonghua Palace; Si submitted ten memorials, his words mostly cutting and urgent.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had long avoided Chonghua Palace; Si submitted ten memorials, many of them sharply worded and urgent.

sentences.zh: 會上召嘉王，思言：「壽皇欲見陛下，亦猶陛下之于嘉王也。」

translations.literal: It happened that the emperor summoned Prince Jia; Si said: “The Retired Emperor wishes to see Your Majesty just as Your Majesty wishes to see Prince Jia.”
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor summoned Prince Jia, Si said, “The Retired Emperor longs to see Your Majesty as much as Your Majesty longs to see Prince Jia.”

sentences.zh: 上為動容。

translations.literal: The emperor was moved in countenance.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was moved.

sentences.zh: 時李皇后浸預政，思進講姜氏會齊侯於濼，因奏：「人主治國必自齊家始，家之不能齊者，不能防其漸也。

translations.literal: At that time Empress Li was gradually interfering in government; Si, lecturing on the Duke of Jiang’s meeting with the Duke of Qi at Luo, thereupon memorialized: “A ruler who governs the realm must begin by ordering the household; one who cannot order the household cannot guard against gradual encroachment.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Li was gradually meddling in affairs of state. Si lectured on the Duke of Jiang’s meeting with the Duke of Qi at Luo and memorialized, “A ruler must put his own house in order before he can govern the realm. Those who cannot keep the household in order cannot check encroachment at its first stirrings.

sentences.zh: 始於褻狎，終於恣橫，卒至於陰陽易位，內外無別，甚則離間父子。

translations.literal: It begins with familiar intimacy, ends in wilful overbearing, and finally reaches the inversion of yin and yang, with no distinction between inner and outer—at the worst, driving father and son apart.
translations.idiomatic: It begins with undue familiarity, ends in brazen overreach, and finally inverts the proper order of inner and outer until there is no distinction at all—in the worst case, driving father and son apart.

sentences.zh: 漢之呂氏，唐之武、韋，幾至亂亡，不但魯莊公也。」

translations.literal: Empress Lü of Han, Wu and Wei of Tang—nearly to disorder and ruin—not only Duke Zhuang of Lu.”
translations.idiomatic: Empress Lü of Han, Wu and Wei of Tang—dynasties nearly brought to ruin—and not only the case of Duke Zhuang of Lu.”

sentences.zh: 上悚然。

translations.literal: The emperor was startled.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was startled.

sentences.zh: 趙汝愚同侍經筵，退語人曰：「讜直如此，吾黨不逮也。」

translations.literal: Zhao Ruyu together attended the classics lecture hall; on withdrawing he told others: “Such candor and rectitude—our faction cannot match it.”
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Ruyu, who shared lecture attendance with him, said afterward, “Such candor and integrity—our faction cannot equal it.”

sentences.zh: 兼權吏部侍郎，出知紹興府。

translations.literal: Concurrently acting vice minister of personnel; sent out as prefect of Shaoxing.
translations.idiomatic: He was made acting vice minister of personnel, then sent out as prefect of Shaoxing.

sentences.zh: 寧宗即位，改婺州，未上，提舉太平興國宮，召除吏部侍郎兼直學士院。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ningzong ascended, he was reassigned to Wuzhou; before assuming office he was made director of the Taiping Xingguo Palace; recalled and appointed vice minister of personnel concurrently director of the Academy of Scholarly Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: When Ningzong ascended he was reassigned to Wuzhou, but before taking up the post was made director of the Taiping Xingguo Palace. Recalled, he was appointed vice minister of personnel with concurrent Hanlin Academy directorship.

sentences.zh: 御史姚愈劾思，出知太平州，歷知泉州，建寧府，皆以言者論去。

translations.literal: Censor Yao Yu impeached Si; he was sent out as prefect of Taiping, and successively served as prefect of Quanzhou and Jianning—all dismissed after critics spoke against him.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Yao Yu impeached Si and he was sent out as prefect of Taiping. He later served as prefect of Quanzhou and Jianning, but was driven from each post by critics.

sentences.zh: 久之，召還，試禮部侍郎兼直學士院。

translations.literal: After a long time he was recalled and made acting vice minister of rites concurrently director of the Academy of Scholarly Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he was recalled and made acting vice minister of rites with concurrent Hanlin Academy directorship.

sentences.zh: 侂胄先以書致殷勤，曰：「國事如此，一世人望，豈宜專以潔己為賢哉？」

translations.literal: Tuozhou first sent a letter expressing warm courtesy, saying: “Affairs of state being as they are, a man of your generation’s esteem—should you make purity of self alone your virtue?”
translations.idiomatic: Han Tuozhou first sent a cordial letter, saying, “Affairs of state are as they are—a man of your generation’s standing—should you make personal purity your only virtue?”

sentences.zh: 思報曰：「但恐方拙，不能徇時好耳。」

translations.literal: Si replied: “I only fear my squareness and clumsiness—I cannot follow the fashions of the age, that is all.”
translations.idiomatic: Si replied, “I only fear I am too square and clumsy to follow the fashions of the age.”

sentences.zh: 時赴召者，未引對先謁侂胄，或勸用近例，思曰：「私門不可登，矧未見君乎？」

translations.literal: At that time those summoned to audience, before facing the throne, first visited Tuozhou; some urged following recent precedent; Si said: “A private house must not be entered—how much less before one has seen the sovereign?”
translations.idiomatic: Those summoned to court then often visited Han Tuozhou before their audience. Some urged him to follow recent precedent, but Si said, “One must not enter a private house—how much less before one has seen the sovereign?”

sentences.zh: 逮入見，首論言路不通：「自呂祖儉謫徙而朝士不敢輸忠，自呂祖泰編竄而布衣不敢極說。

translations.literal: When he entered audience he first discussed the blocked remonstrance path: “Since Lu Zujian was banished and relocated, court officials dare not offer loyalty; since Lu Zutai was dispatched to the frontier, commoners in plain cloth dare not speak to the limit.
translations.idiomatic: When he entered audience he spoke first of the blocked remonstrance path: “Since Lu Zujian was banished and relocated, court officials dare not speak loyally; since Lu Zutai was dispatched to the frontier, commoners dare not speak their minds fully.

sentences.zh: 膠庠之士欲有吐露，恐之以去籍，諭之以呈槁，誰肯披肝瀝膽，觸冒威尊？

translations.literal: Students of the imperial academy wishing to speak out are threatened with expulsion from the rolls and instructed to submit drafts—who would lay bare heart and liver and offend august authority?
translations.idiomatic: Academy students who wish to speak out are threatened with expulsion and told to submit drafts in advance—who would lay bare heart and liver and offend the throne?

sentences.zh: 近者北伐之舉，僅有一二人言其不可，如使未舉之前，相繼力爭之，更加詳審，不致輕動。」

translations.literal: The recent northern expedition—only one or two spoke that it should not be undertaken; if before it was launched they had argued forcefully in succession, with greater deliberation, it would not have been lightly set in motion.”
translations.idiomatic: On the recent northern expedition only one or two spoke against it. Had they argued forcefully in succession before it was launched, with greater deliberation, the court would not have moved so rashly.”

sentences.zh: 又言：「蘇師旦贓以巨萬計，胡不黥戮以謝三軍？

translations.literal: He also said: “Su Shidan’s embezzlement runs to tens of thousands—why not brand and execute him to answer the three armies?
translations.idiomatic: He also said, “Su Shidan’s embezzlement runs to vast sums—why not brand and execute him to answer the armies?

sentences.zh: 皇甫斌喪師襄漢，李爽敗績淮甸，秦世輔潰散蜀道，皆罪大罰輕。」

translations.literal: Huangfu Bin lost the army in Xiang and Han; Li Shuang was defeated on the Huai frontier; Qin Shipu scattered troops on the Sichuan route—all great crimes with light punishments.”
translations.idiomatic: Huangfu Bin lost his army in Xiang and Han; Li Shuang was defeated on the Huai frontier; Qin Shipu’s forces scattered on the Sichuan route—all grave crimes punished lightly.”

sentences.zh: 又言：「士大夫寡廉鮮恥，列拜於勢要之門，甚者匍匐門竇，稱門生不足，稱恩坐、恩主甚至於恩父者，諛文豐賂，又在所不論也。」

translations.literal: He also said: “Scholar-officials lack integrity and shame—they line up to bow at the gates of the powerful; some crawl at the door-sill, calling themselves disciples insufficiently, calling themselves favored seat, favored master, even favored father—fulsome prose and rich bribes go without saying.”
translations.idiomatic: He also said, “Scholar-officials lack integrity and shame. They queue to bow at the gates of the powerful; some crawl at the threshold, calling themselves disciples, favored seat, favored master, even favored father—fulsome prose and rich bribes scarcely need mention.”

sentences.zh: 侂胄聞之大怒。

translations.literal: Tuozhou heard this and was greatly enraged.
translations.idiomatic: Han Tuozhou heard this and was furious.

sentences.zh: 思既退，謂侂胄曰：「公明有餘而聰不足：堂中剖決如流，此明有餘；

translations.literal: After Si had withdrawn, he said to Tuozhou: “Your Lordship has surplus clearness but insufficient discernment: judgments in the hall flow like water—this is surplus clearness;
translations.idiomatic: After withdrawing, Si told Han Tuozhou, “Your Lordship has surplus clarity but insufficient discernment. Judgments in the hall flow like water—that is surplus clarity;

sentences.zh: 為蘇師旦蒙蔽，此聰不足也。

translations.literal: to be hoodwinked by Su Shidan—this is insufficient discernment.
translations.idiomatic: to be hoodwinked by Su Shidan—that is insufficient discernment.

sentences.zh: 周筠與師旦並為姦利，師旦已敗，筠尚在，人言平章騎虎不下之勢，此李林甫、楊國忠晚節也。」

translations.literal: Zhou Jun and Shidan alike committed corrupt profit; Shidan has already fallen but Jun remains—people say the chief councilor is in the posture of one who mounted a tiger and cannot dismount—this is the late career of Li Linfu and Yang Guozhong.”
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Jun and Shidan alike pursued corrupt profit. Shidan has already fallen but Jun remains—people say the chief councilor rides a tiger and cannot dismount. This is the late career of Li Linfu and Yang Guozhong.”

sentences.zh: 侂胄悚然曰：「聞所未聞！」

translations.literal: Tuozhou started and said: “What I have never heard before!”
translations.idiomatic: Han Tuozhou started and said, “I have never heard the like!”

sentences.zh: 司諫毛憲劾思，予祠。

translations.literal: Remonstrance official Mao Xian impeached Si; he was given a temple post.
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrance official Mao Xian impeached Si, and he was given a temple sinecure.

sentences.zh: 侂胄殛，復召，首對，乞用淳熙例，令太子開議事堂，閑習機政。

translations.literal: After Tuozhou was executed, Si was recalled; at his first audience he requested using the Chunxi precedent of having the crown prince open a council hall to familiarize himself with state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: After Han Tuozhou was executed Si was recalled. At his first audience he asked to follow the Chunxi precedent and have the crown prince open a council hall to familiarize himself with affairs of state.

sentences.zh: 又言：「侂胄擅命，凡事取內批特旨，當以為戒。」

translations.literal: He also said: “Tuozhou arrogated command—taking inner drafts and special edicts for all affairs—let this be taken as a warning.”
translations.idiomatic: He also said, “Han Tuozhou arrogated command, taking inner drafts and special edicts for every affair—let that be a warning.”

sentences.zh: 除權兵部尚書兼侍讀。

translations.literal: He was appointed acting minister of war concurrently lecturing attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed acting minister of war with concurrent lecturing attendant.

sentences.zh: 求對，言：「大權方歸，所當防微，一有干預端倪，必且仍蹈覆轍。

translations.literal: He requested audience and said: “Great power has just returned—one must guard against the slightest beginning; any trace of interference and the overturned cart’s track will again be trodden.
translations.idiomatic: He requested audience and said, “Great power has just returned to proper channels—one must guard against the slightest encroachment. Any sign of interference and the old path will be trodden again.

sentences.zh: 厥今有更化之名，無更化之實。

translations.literal: At present there is the name of renewal but not the reality of renewal.
translations.idiomatic: Today there is the name of renewal but not the reality of renewal.

sentences.zh: 今侂胄既誅，而國人之言猶有未靖者，蓋以樞臣猶兼宮賓，不時宣召，宰執當同班同對，樞臣亦當遠權，以息外議。」

translations.literal: Now that Tuozhou has been executed yet the talk of the realm’s people is still unsettled—it is because the Bureau chief still concurrently holds palace attendant rank and is summoned at irregular times; chief councilors should attend in the same cohort and same audience; the Bureau chief should also keep distant from power to quiet outside talk.”
translations.idiomatic: Now that Han Tuozhou has been executed, public talk is still unsettled because the Bureau chief still holds palace attendant rank and is summoned at irregular times. Chief councilors should attend in the same cohort and face the throne together, and the Bureau chief should keep his distance from power to quiet outside criticism.”

sentences.zh: 樞臣，謂史彌遠也。

translations.literal: The Bureau chief—meaning Shi Miyuan.
translations.idiomatic: The Bureau chief meant Shi Miyuan.

sentences.zh: 金人求侂胄函首，命廷臣集議，思謂有傷國體。

translations.literal: The Jin requested Tuozhou’s head in a box; the court ordered ministers to deliberate jointly; Si said it would injure national dignity.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin demanded Han Tuozhou’s head in a box, the court ordered ministers to deliberate jointly. Si said it would injure national dignity.

sentences.zh: 徙禮部尚書。

translations.literal: He was transferred to minister of rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 史彌遠擬除兩從官，參政錢象祖不與聞。

translations.literal: Shi Miyuan planned to appoint two junior officials; Vice Premier Qian Xiangzu was not consulted.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Miyuan planned to appoint two junior officials without consulting Vice Premier Qian Xiangzu.

sentences.zh: 思言：「奏擬除目，宰執當同進，比專聽侂胄，權有所偏，覆轍可鑒。」

translations.literal: Si said: “When memorializing proposed appointments, chief councilors should advance together—compared with listening solely to Tuozhou, power was partial; the overturned cart is a warning.”
translations.idiomatic: Si said, “When proposed appointments are memorialized, chief councilors should advance together. Listening solely to Han Tuozhou skewed power—the overturned cart is a warning.”

sentences.zh: 既而史彌遠上章自辨，思求去，上留之。

translations.literal: Soon Shi Miyuan submitted a memorial in self-defense; Si requested to leave; the emperor kept him.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Shi Miyuan submitted a memorial in self-defense. Si asked to resign, but the emperor kept him.

sentences.zh: 思乞對，言：「前日論樞臣獨班，恐蹈往轍，宗社堪再壞耶？

translations.literal: Si requested audience and said: “The other day I spoke of the Bureau chief attending alone—I fear treading the old path—can the altars of state bear ruin twice?
translations.idiomatic: Si requested audience and said, “The other day I spoke of the Bureau chief attending alone. I fear we are treading the old path—can the altars of state bear ruin twice?

sentences.zh: 宜親擢臺諫，以革權臣之弊，並任宰輔，以鑒專擅之失。」

translations.literal: One should personally elevate censorate and remonstrance officials to reform the evils of powerful ministers, and employ chief and associate councilors together to take warning from monopolization of power.”
translations.idiomatic: The emperor should personally elevate censorate and remonstrance officials to reform the evils of powerful ministers, and employ chief and associate councilors together to take warning from monopolization of power.”

sentences.zh: 彌遠懷恚，思請去益力，以寶謨閣直學士知鎮江府，移福州。

translations.literal: Miyuan harbored resentment; Si’s requests to leave grew stronger; he was made Hanlin academician of the Hall for Expounding Principles and prefect of Zhenjiang, then transferred to Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Miyuan harbored resentment. Si pressed harder to resign and was made Hanlin academician of the Hall for Expounding Principles and prefect of Zhenjiang, then transferred to Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 彌遠拜右丞相，陳晦草制用「昆命元龜」語，思歎曰：「董賢為大司馬，冊文有『允執厥中』一言，蕭咸以為堯禪舜之文，長老見之，莫不心懼。

translations.literal: Miyuan was appointed right chief councilor; Chen Hui drafted the appointment edict using the phrase “Kun orders the primordial tortoise”; Si sighed and said: “When Dong Xian became grand marshal, the appointment text had the phrase ‘faithfully hold the center’; Xiao Xian took it for the text of Yao yielding to Shun—when elders saw it, none did not fear in heart.
translations.idiomatic: When Miyuan was appointed right chief councilor, Chen Hui drafted the edict using the phrase “Kun orders the primordial tortoise.” Si sighed and said, “When Dong Xian became grand marshal, the appointment text contained ‘faithfully hold the center.’ Xiao Xian took it for the language of Yao yielding to Shun, and every elder who read it was struck with fear.

sentences.zh: 今制詞所引，此舜、禹揖遜也。

translations.literal: The language cited in today’s edict—this is the yielding deference of Shun and Yu.
translations.idiomatic: The language cited in today’s edict is the yielding deference of Shun and Yu.

sentences.zh: 天下有如蕭咸者讀之，得不大駭乎？」

translations.literal: If there are readers like Xiao Xian under Heaven, will they not be greatly appalled?”
translations.idiomatic: If readers like Xiao Xian exist anywhere under Heaven, will they not be appalled?”

sentences.zh: 仍上省牘，請貼改麻制。

translations.literal: He also submitted a document to the Secretariat requesting pasted correction of the hemp edict.
translations.idiomatic: He also submitted a document to the Secretariat requesting correction of the hemp appointment edict.

sentences.zh: 詔下分析，彌遠遂除晦殿中侍御史，即劾思藩臣僭論麻制，鐫職而罷，自是不復起矣。

translations.literal: An edict went down for analysis; Miyuan then appointed Hui palace censor and immediately impeached Si—a border vassal overstepping in discussing the hemp edict—stripped of office and dismissed; from then on he was never reappointed.
translations.idiomatic: An edict went down for analysis. Miyuan then appointed Hui palace censor, who immediately impeached Si—a border official overstepping in discussing the hemp edict. Si was stripped of rank and dismissed, and from then on was never reappointed.

sentences.zh: 久之，除寶文閣學士，提舉嵩山崇福宮。

translations.literal: After a long time he was made academician of the Hall for Treasuring Culture and director of the Songshan Chongfu Palace.
translations.idiomatic: After a long interval he was made academician of the Hall for Treasuring Culture and director of the Songshan Chongfu Palace.

sentences.zh: 嘉定十三年卒，諡「文節」。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Jiading he died; posthumous title “Cultured and Restrained.”
translations.idiomatic: He died in the thirteenth year of Jiading and was posthumously titled “Cultured and Restrained.”

sentences.zh: 宇文紹節

translations.literal: Yuwen Shaojie
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Shaojie

sentences.zh: 宇文紹節，字挺臣，成都廣都人。

translations.literal: Yuwen Shaojie, courtesy name Tingchen, was a native of Guangdu in Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Shaojie, whose courtesy name was Tingchen, came from Guangdu in Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 祖虛中，簽書樞密院事。

translations.literal: His grandfather Xuzhong was junior signatory of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Xuzhong served as junior signatory of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 父師瑗，顯謨閣待制。

translations.literal: His father Shiyuan was Hanlin attendant of the Hall for Manifest Strategy.
translations.idiomatic: His father Shiyuan was Hanlin attendant of the Hall for Manifest Strategy.

sentences.zh: 父子皆以使北死，無子，孝宗湣之，命其族子紹節為之後，補官仕州縣。

translations.literal: Father and son both died on mission north; having no son, Emperor Xiaozong took pity and ordered a clansman Shaojie to succeed them; given office he served in prefectures and counties.
translations.idiomatic: Father and son both died on missions to the north. Having no heir, Xiaozong took pity and ordered a clansman, Shaojie, to succeed them. Given office, he served in prefectures and counties.

sentences.zh: 九年，第進士。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he placed as a jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 累遷寶謨閣待制、知廬州。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Hanlin attendant of the Hall for Expounding Principles and prefect of Luzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Hanlin attendant of the Hall for Expounding Principles and prefect of Luzhou.

sentences.zh: 時侂胄方議用兵，紹節至郡，議修築古城，創造砦柵，專為固圉計。

translations.literal: At that time Tuozhou was discussing using troops; when Shaojie reached the prefecture he proposed repairing old walls and creating stockades and palisades, solely planning to secure the defense perimeter.
translations.idiomatic: Han Tuozhou was then debating war. When Shaojie reached his prefecture he proposed repairing old walls and building stockades and palisades, planning solely to strengthen defenses.

sentences.zh: 淮西轉運判官鄧友龍譖于侂胄，謂紹節但為城守，徒耗財力，無益於事。

translations.literal: Huai-Xi transport vice commissioner Deng Youlong slandered him to Tuozhou, saying Shaojie only held cities and wasted finances and manpower without benefit to the enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: Huai-Xi transport vice commissioner Deng Youlong slandered him to Han Tuozhou, saying Shaojie merely held cities, wasting money and manpower to no purpose.

sentences.zh: 侂胄以書讓紹節，紹節復書謂：「公有復讐之志，而無復讐之略；

translations.literal: Tuozhou sent a letter rebuking Shaojie; Shaojie replied: “Your Lordship has the will to take revenge but not the strategy for revenge;
translations.idiomatic: Han Tuozhou sent a letter rebuking Shaojie. Shaojie replied, “Your Lordship has the will to take revenge but not the strategy for revenge;

sentences.zh: 有開邊之害，而無開邊之利。

translations.literal: the harm of opening the frontier but not its benefit.
translations.idiomatic: the harm of opening the frontier but not its benefit.

sentences.zh: 不量國力，浪為進取計，非所敢知。」

translations.literal: Not measuring national strength and recklessly plotting advance—this is beyond what I dare know.”
translations.idiomatic: Recklessly plotting advance without measuring national strength is beyond what I dare understand.”

sentences.zh: 侂胄得書不樂，乃以李爽代紹節，召還，為兵部侍郎兼中書舍人兼直學士院，以寶文閣待制知鎮江府。

translations.literal: Tuozhou received the letter displeased; Li Shuang replaced Shaojie; he was recalled and made vice minister of war concurrently drafter of the Secretariat and director of the Academy of Scholarly Worthies; as Hanlin attendant of the Hall for Treasuring Culture he served as prefect of Zhenjiang.
translations.idiomatic: Han Tuozhou received the letter displeased. Li Shuang replaced Shaojie, who was recalled and made vice minister of war with concurrent Secretariat drafter and Hanlin Academy directorship, then sent out as Hanlin attendant of the Hall for Treasuring Culture and prefect of Zhenjiang.

sentences.zh: 吳曦據蜀，趣紹節赴闕，任以西討之事。

translations.literal: Wu Xi held Sichuan; Shaojie was urgently summoned to court and charged with the western punitive campaign.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu Xi seized Sichuan, Shaojie was urgently summoned to court and charged with the western punitive campaign.

sentences.zh: 紹節至，謂大臣曰：「今進攻，則瞿唐一關，彼必固守；

translations.literal: When Shaojie arrived he told the chief ministers: “If we attack now, at the single pass of Qutang they will surely hold firm;
translations.idiomatic: When Shaojie arrived he told the chief ministers, “If we attack now, at Qutang Pass alone they will surely hold firm;

sentences.zh: 若駐軍荊南，徒損威望。

translations.literal: if we station troops at Jingnan, we only diminish prestige.
translations.idiomatic: if we station troops at Jingnan we only diminish our prestige.

sentences.zh: 聞隨軍轉運安丙者素懷忠義，若授以密旨，必能討賊成功。」

translations.literal: I hear the campaign transport officer An Bing has long harbored loyalty and righteousness—if entrusted with a secret edict he can surely succeed in punishing the rebel.”
translations.idiomatic: I hear that campaign transport officer An Bing has long harbored loyalty and righteousness. Entrust him with a secret edict and he can surely succeed in punishing the rebel.”

sentences.zh: 大臣用其言，遣丙所親以帛書達上意，丙卒誅曦。

translations.literal: The chief ministers adopted his view; they sent An Bing’s close associate with a silk letter conveying the emperor’s intent; Bing ultimately executed Xi.
translations.idiomatic: The chief ministers adopted his plan and sent a close associate of An Bing with a silk letter conveying the emperor’s intent. Bing ultimately executed Xi.

sentences.zh: 權兵部尚書，未幾，除華文閣學士、湖北京西宣撫使、知江陵府。

translations.literal: Acting minister of war; soon appointed academician of the Hall for Refining Culture, Hubei Jingxi pacification commissioner, and prefect of Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: He served as acting minister of war and soon was appointed academician of the Hall for Refining Culture, Hubei Jingxi pacification commissioner, and prefect of Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 統制官高悅在戍所，肆為殺掠，遠近苦之。

translations.literal: Commanding officer Gao Yue at the garrison wantonly killed and plundered; near and far suffered.
translations.idiomatic: Commanding officer Gao Yue at the garrison wantonly killed and plundered, and the region suffered.

sentences.zh: 紹節召置帳前，收其部曲。

translations.literal: Shaojie summoned him before his tent and confiscated his troops.
translations.idiomatic: Shaojie summoned him before his tent and confiscated his troops.

sentences.zh: 俄有訴悅縱所部為寇者，紹節杖殺之，兵民皆歡。

translations.literal: Soon someone complained that Yue let his troops run as bandits; Shaojie had him beaten to death; soldiers and civilians rejoiced.
translations.idiomatic: Soon someone complained that Yue had let his troops run as bandits. Shaojie had him beaten to death, and soldiers and civilians rejoiced.

sentences.zh: 升寶文閣學士，試吏部尚書，尋除端明殿學士、簽書樞密院事。

translations.literal: Promoted to academician of the Hall for Treasuring Culture and acting minister of personnel; soon appointed academician of the Hall of Illustrious Virtue and junior signatory of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to academician of the Hall for Treasuring Culture and acting minister of personnel, then soon appointed academician of the Hall of Illustrious Virtue and junior signatory of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 安丙宣撫四川，或言丙有異志，語聞，廷臣欲易丙。

translations.literal: An Bing pacified Sichuan; some said Bing had divergent intentions; word reached the court; ministers wished to replace Bing.
translations.idiomatic: An Bing was pacification commissioner of Sichuan. When word reached court that he harbored divergent intentions, ministers wished to replace him.

sentences.zh: 紹節曰：「方誅曦初，安丙一搖足，全蜀非國家有，顧不以此時為利，今乃有他耶？

translations.literal: Shaojie said: “Just when Xi was first punished—had An Bing shifted one foot, all Sichuan would not belong to the state; he clearly did not seize this moment for profit—would he have other designs now?
translations.idiomatic: Shaojie said, “Just after Xi was punished, had An Bing shifted one foot all Sichuan would no longer have belonged to the state. He clearly did not seize that moment for profit—would he harbor other designs now?

sentences.zh: 紹節願以百口保丙。」

translations.literal: Shaojie wished to guarantee Bing with a hundred mouths.”
translations.idiomatic: Shaojie offered to guarantee Bing with a hundred lives.”

sentences.zh: 丙卒不易。

translations.literal: Bing was ultimately not replaced.
translations.idiomatic: An Bing was ultimately not replaced.

sentences.zh: 朝廷於蜀事多所咨訪，紹節審而後言，皆周悉事情。

translations.literal: The court frequently consulted on Sichuan affairs; Shaojie spoke only after careful review—all exhaustively knowing the circumstances.
translations.idiomatic: The court frequently consulted him on Sichuan affairs. Shaojie spoke only after careful review, and his answers were thorough.

sentences.zh: 嘉定六年正月甲午卒，訃聞，上嗟悼，為改日朝享。

translations.literal: On jiawu day of the first month of the sixth year of Jiading he died; when death was reported the emperor sighed in grief and changed the day of court audience.
translations.idiomatic: He died on jiawu day of the first month of Jiading 6. When word reached the throne the emperor sighed in grief and changed the day of court audience.

sentences.zh: 進資政殿學士致仕，又贈七官為少師，非常典也。

translations.literal: He was advanced to grand academician of the Hall for Assisting Governance as retired; also posthumously given seven ranks to grand mentor—an extraordinary honor.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously advanced to grand academician of the Hall for Assisting Governance as retired, and given seven additional ranks to grand mentor—an extraordinary honor.

sentences.zh: 諡曰「忠惠」。

translations.literal: Posthumous title “Loyal and Generous.”
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously titled “Loyal and Generous.”

sentences.zh: 李蘩，字清叔，崇慶晉原人。

translations.literal: Li Fan, courtesy name Qingshu, was a native of Jinyuan in Chongqing.
translations.idiomatic: Li Fan, whose courtesy name was Qingshu, came from Jinyuan in Chongqing.

sentences.zh: 第進士，為隆州判官，攝綿州。

translations.literal: He placed as a jinshi; served as vice magistrate of Longzhou and acting prefect of Mianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After passing the jinshi examination he served as vice magistrate of Longzhou and acting prefect of Mianzhou.

sentences.zh: 歲祲，出義倉穀賤糶之，而以錢貸下戶，又聽民以茅秸易米，作粥及褚衣，親衣食之，活十萬人。

translations.literal: In a lean year he released ever-normal granary grain sold cheaply, lent cash to lower households, allowed people to exchange straw for rice, made porridge and cotton clothing, personally fed and clothed them—saving a hundred thousand lives.
translations.idiomatic: In a lean year he released ever-normal granary grain and sold it cheaply, lent cash to poorer households, and allowed people to exchange straw for rice. He made porridge and cotton clothing and personally fed and clothed the needy, saving a hundred thousand lives.

sentences.zh: 明年又饑，邛蜀彭漢、成都盜賊蜂起，綿獨安堵。

translations.literal: The next year famine came again; in Qiong, Shu, Peng, Han, and Chengdu bandits swarmed—Mian alone remained tranquil.
translations.idiomatic: The next year famine returned. Bandits swarmed in Qiong, Shu, Peng, Han, and Chengdu, but Mian alone remained tranquil.

sentences.zh: 知永康軍，移利州，提點成都路刑獄兼提舉常平。

translations.literal: Prefect of Yongkang Army; transferred to Lizhou; judicial intendant of Chengdu circuit concurrently Ever-Normal intendant.
translations.idiomatic: He served as prefect of Yongkang Army, then transferred to Lizhou as judicial intendant of Chengdu circuit and Ever-Normal intendant.

sentences.zh: 歲凶，先事發廩蠲租，所活百七十萬人。

translations.literal: In bad harvest years he opened granaries and remitted rent beforehand—saving one million seven hundred thousand lives.
translations.idiomatic: In bad harvest years he opened granaries and remitted rent in advance, saving one million seven hundred thousand lives.

sentences.zh: 知興元府、安撫利州東路。

translations.literal: Prefect of Xingyuan and pacification commissioner of eastern Lizhou route.
translations.idiomatic: He served as prefect of Xingyuan and pacification commissioner of the eastern Lizhou route.

sentences.zh: 漢中久饑，劍外和糴在州者獨多，蘩嘗匹馬行阡陌間訪求民瘼，有老嫗進曰：「民所以饑者，和糴病之也。」

translations.literal: Hanzhong had long suffered famine; among prefectures outside Jian, hedged purchases stored locally were uniquely heavy; Fan once rode alone through fields seeking the people’s afflictions; an old woman came forward and said: “The reason the people starve is that hedged purchase harms them.”
translations.idiomatic: Hanzhong had long suffered famine, and among prefectures beyond Jian it alone stored unusually large hedged-purchase reserves. Fan once rode alone through the fields seeking the people’s grievances. An old woman came forward and said, “The people starve because hedged purchase harms them.”

sentences.zh: 泣數行下。

translations.literal: She wept, tears streaming down.
translations.idiomatic: She wept, tears streaming down her face.

sentences.zh: 蘩感其言，奏免之，民大悅。

translations.literal: Fan was moved by her words, memorialized for exemption, and the people greatly rejoiced.
translations.idiomatic: Moved by her words, Fan memorialized for exemption, and the people rejoiced.

sentences.zh: 徙倉部員外郎，總領四川賦財、軍馬、錢糧，升郎中。

translations.literal: Transferred to vice director of granaries; overall director of Sichuan revenue, horses, cash, and grain; promoted to director.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to vice director of granaries and made overall director of Sichuan revenue, horses, cash, and grain, then promoted to director.

sentences.zh: 淳熙三年，廷臣上言：「四川歲糴軍糧，名為和糴，實科糴也。」

translations.literal: In the third year of Chunxi court officials memorialized: “Sichuan’s annual purchase of army grain—called hedged purchase, in fact it is compulsory purchase.”
translations.idiomatic: In Chunxi 3 court officials memorialized, “Sichuan’s annual purchase of army grain is called hedged purchase, but in fact it is compulsory purchase.”

sentences.zh: 詔制置使范成大同蘩相度以聞，蘩奏：「諸州歲糴六十萬石，若從官糴，歲約百萬緡，如於經費之中斟酌損益，變科糴為官糴，貴賤眂時，不使虧毫忽之價；

translations.literal: An edict ordered Pacification Commissioner Fan Chengda and Fan jointly to assess and report; Fan memorialized: “Prefectures annually purchase six hundred thousand shi—if following official purchase, about one million strings per year; if within the regular budget one adjusts increase and decrease, converting compulsory purchase to official purchase, high and low according to the times, not allowing the slightest loss in price;
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Pacification Commissioner Fan Chengda and Fan jointly to assess the matter and report. Fan memorialized, “Prefectures annually purchase six hundred thousand shi of grain. Under official purchase the cost runs to about one million strings per year. If within the regular budget one adjusts increase and decrease, converting compulsory purchase to official purchase and setting prices high or low according to the times so that not the slightest loss is imposed;

sentences.zh: 出納眂量，勿務取圭撮之贏，則軍不乏興，民不加賦。」

translations.literal: In receipts and disbursements take careful measure; do not strive to seize profit of a spoonful or pinch—then the army will not lack supplies and the people will not bear added levies.”
translations.idiomatic: In receipts and disbursements take careful measure; do not chase spoonful profits—then the army will not lack supplies and the people will not bear added levies.”

sentences.zh: 乃書「利民十一事」上之。

translations.literal: He thereupon wrote “Eleven Matters for Benefiting the People” and presented it.
translations.idiomatic: He then submitted “Eleven Measures for Benefiting the People.”

sentences.zh: 前後凡三年，蘩上奏疏者十有三，而天子降詔難問者凡八，訖如其議。

translations.literal: Over three years in all Fan memorialized thirteen times, and the Son of Heaven eight times sent edicts with difficult questions; in the end it followed his proposal.
translations.idiomatic: Over three years Fan memorialized thirteen times; the emperor eight times sent edicts pressing hard questions—and in the end adopted his plan.

sentences.zh: 民既樂與官為市，遠邇歡趨，軍餉坐給，而田里免科糴，始知有生之樂。

translations.literal: Once the people were glad to trade with the government, near and far rushed joyfully; army provisions were supplied sitting still, and in the fields compulsory purchase was remitted—only then did they know the joy of being alive.
translations.idiomatic: Once the people were glad to trade with the government, near and far flocked in; army rations were met without strain, and the fields were freed from compulsory purchase—only then did they know the joy of life.

sentences.zh: 會歲大稔，米價頓賤，父老以為三十年所無。

translations.literal: It happened that the year was greatly abundant and rice prices suddenly fell; the elders held it unmatched in thirty years.
translations.idiomatic: That year brought a great harvest and rice prices plunged—the elders said they had not seen the like in thirty years.

sentences.zh: 梁、洋間繪蘩像祠之。

translations.literal: Between Liang and Yang they painted Fan’s image and enshrined him.
translations.idiomatic: Between Liang and Yang they painted Fan’s portrait and set up shrines to him.

sentences.zh: 范成大驛疏言：「關外麥熟，倍于常年，實由罷糴，民力稍紓，得以盡于農畝。」

translations.literal: Fan Chengda by courier memorial said: “Wheat beyond the passes is ripe, double the normal year—this truly comes from ending purchase; the people’s strength is slightly eased and they can devote themselves fully to the fields.”
translations.idiomatic: Fan Chengda reported by courier, “Wheat beyond the passes is ripe at twice the usual yield—truly because purchase was ended, the people’s strength eased, and they could devote themselves fully to the fields.”

sentences.zh: 孝宗覽之曰：「免和糴一年，田間和氣若此，乃知民力不可重困也。」

translations.literal: Xiaozong read it and said: “Exempting hedged purchase for one year—such harmony in the fields—now I know the people’s strength must not be heavily burdened.”
translations.idiomatic: Xiaozong read it and said, “One year without hedged purchase—and such harmony in the fields. Now I know the people’s strength must not be crushed.”

sentences.zh: 擢蘩守太府少卿。

translations.literal: Fan was promoted to vice director of the Court of the Imperial Treasury.
translations.idiomatic: Fan was promoted to vice director of the Court of the Imperial Treasury.

sentences.zh: 范成大召見，孝宗首問：「糴事可久行否？」

translations.literal: Fan Chengda was summoned for audience; Xiaozong first asked: “Can the purchase affair be carried on long?”
translations.idiomatic: When Fan Chengda was summoned, Xiaozong’s first question was, “Can this purchase system continue long-term?”

sentences.zh: 成大奏：「李蘩以身任此事，臣以身保李蘩。」

translations.literal: Chengda memorialized: “Li Fan bears this matter with his person; your servant vouches for Li Fan with his person.”
translations.idiomatic: Chengda replied, “Li Fan stakes his person on this matter; I stake my person on Li Fan.”

sentences.zh: 孝宗大悅，曰：「是大不可得李蘩也。」

translations.literal: Xiaozong was greatly pleased and said: “Such a man—Li Fan cannot be obtained.”
translations.idiomatic: Xiaozong was delighted and said, “A man like this—Li Fan is irreplaceable.”

sentences.zh: 上意方向用，而蘩亦欲奏蠲鹽酒和買之弊，以盡滌民害。

translations.literal: The emperor’s intent was to employ him further, and Fan also wished to memorialize to remit the abuses of salt, wine, and harmonized purchase, to wash away the people’s harms completely.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor meant to employ him further, and Fan also planned to memorialize remitting abuses in salt, wine, and harmonized purchase to cleanse the people’s burdens entirely.

sentences.zh: 會有疾，卒。

translations.literal: It happened that he fell ill and died.
translations.idiomatic: But he fell ill and died.

sentences.zh: 詔以蘩能官，致仕恩外特與遺表，擇一人庶官，前此所未有。

translations.literal: An edict, because Fan was capable in office, beyond retirement grace specially granted a posthumous memorial table to select one person for a common office—unprecedented before this.
translations.idiomatic: Because Fan had served capably, an edict beyond ordinary retirement grace specially granted a posthumous memorial privilege to name one commoner for office—unprecedented.

sentences.zh: 初，蘩宰眉山，校成都漕試，念吳氏世襲兵柄必稔蜀亂，發策云：「久假人以兵柄，未有不為患者。

translations.literal: At first, when Fan was magistrate of Meishan, he graded the Chengdu transport examination; mindful that the Wu clan’s hereditary grip on military power would ripen chaos in Shu, he set an examination topic saying: “To lend others military power for long—none have not become a trouble.
translations.idiomatic: Early on, as magistrate of Meishan, Fan graded the Chengdu transport examination. Mindful that the Wu clan’s hereditary grip on arms would ripen Shu’s chaos, he set a topic: “To lend others military power for long has never failed to breed trouble.

sentences.zh: 以武、宣之明，不能銷大臣握兵之禍；

translations.literal: With the brilliance of Emperor Wu and Emperor Xuan of Han, they could not dissolve the calamity of great ministers holding troops;
translations.idiomatic: For all the brilliance of Han Emperors Wu and Xuan, they could not dissolve the calamity of great ministers holding troops;

sentences.zh: 以憲、武之烈，不能收藩鎮握兵之權。

translations.literal: with the fierceness of Emperor Xian and Emperor Wu of Tang, they could not recover the military power held by frontier commissioners.
translations.idiomatic: for all the fierceness of Tang Emperors Xian and Wu, they could not recover the arms held by frontier commissioners.

sentences.zh: 危劉氏、殲唐室，鮮不由此。」

translations.literal: Endangering the Liu house and destroying the Tang realm—few have not proceeded from this.”
translations.idiomatic: Endangering the Liu house and destroying the Tang realm—few catastrophes have not sprung from this.”

sentences.zh: 吳挺以為怨。

translations.literal: Wu Ting took it as resentment against him.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Ting took it as a personal affront.

sentences.zh: 後蘩總餉事，挺謬奏軍食粗惡，孝宗以問蘩，蘩緘其樣以進，挺之妄遂窮。

translations.literal: Later when Fan oversaw provisions, Ting falsely memorialized that army food was coarse and foul; Xiaozong asked Fan; Fan sealed the sample and presented it, and Ting’s falsehood was thereby exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Fan oversaw provisions, Ting falsely reported that army rations were coarse and foul. Xiaozong asked Fan, who sealed a sample and presented it—exposing Ting’s lie.

sentences.zh: 逾三十年，吳曦竟以蜀叛，安丙既誅曦，每語人云：「吾等焦頭爛額耳，孰如李公先見者乎？」

translations.literal: More than thirty years later Wu Xi ultimately rebelled in Shu; after An Bing had executed Xi, he often said to others: “We merely scorched our heads and blistered our brows—who was like Lord Li’s foresight?”
translations.idiomatic: More than thirty years later Wu Xi rebelled in Shu. After An Bing executed him, he often said, “We merely scorched our heads and blistered our brows—who matched Lord Li’s foresight?”

sentences.zh: 蘩講學臨政皆有源委，所著書十八種，有《桃溪集》一百卷。

translations.literal: Fan’s lecturing and governing both had root and branch; books he authored numbered eighteen kinds, including Collected Works from Peach Brook in one hundred juan.
translations.idiomatic: Fan’s scholarship and governance alike had depth and coherence. He authored eighteen works, including Collected Works from Peach Brook in one hundred juan.

sentences.zh: 論曰：余端禮平時論議剴正，及為相，受制于韓侂胄，雖有志扶掖善類，而不得以直，遂頗不免君子之論。

translations.literal: The appraisal says: Yu Duanli in ordinary times was incisive and upright in discussion; when he became chief councilor he was constrained by Han Tuozhou—though he had the will to support worthy men, he could not be straight, and thus could not quite escape criticism from gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: The appraisal says: Yu Duanli’s ordinary discourse was incisive and upright, but as chief councilor he was constrained by Han Tuozhou. Though he wished to support worthy men, he could not act straight—and thus did not quite escape gentlemen’s criticism.

sentences.zh: 若李壁、丘崈皆諫侂胄以輕兵召釁之失，及其決意用師，命葉適草詔不從，而壁獨當筆焉，何其所見後先舛迕哉！

translations.literal: As for Li Bi and Qiu Chong, both admonished Tuozhou on the error of lightly using troops and inviting provocation—yet when he resolved to use armies and ordered Ye Shi to draft the edict, Shi did not comply while Bi alone took up the brush—how could their views before and after be so at odds!
translations.idiomatic: Li Bi and Qiu Chong both warned Tuozhou against lightly using troops and inviting war—yet when he resolved on war and ordered Ye Shi to draft the expedition edict, Ye refused while Bi alone took up the brush. How could their views be so at odds!

sentences.zh: 附會之罪，壁固無以逭於公論矣。

translations.literal: The crime of currying favor—Bi indeed cannot escape public discourse.
translations.idiomatic: On the charge of currying favor, Bi could not escape public judgment.

sentences.zh: 倪思直辭劘主，又屢觸權臣，三黜不變其風概，有可尚焉。

translations.literal: Ni Si’s blunt words admonished the ruler; he again and again offended powerful ministers; thrice demoted, he did not change his bearing—there is something to esteem.
translations.idiomatic: Ni Si admonished the ruler in blunt terms, repeatedly offended powerful ministers, and was thrice demoted without changing his bearing—something to esteem.

sentences.zh: 李蘩所至能舉荒政，蠲苛賦，亦庶幾古所謂惠人也。

translations.literal: Wherever Li Fan arrived he could raise famine relief policies and remit harsh levies—he also approximates what antiquity called a man of kindness.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever Li Fan served he could mount famine relief and remit harsh levies—he too approximates what antiquity called a man of kindness.
